import type { ConfirmationRequest } from '../../ui/types.js';
import type { ExtensionConfig } from '../extension.js';
import { debugLogger, type SkillDefinition } from '@google/gemini-cli-core';
import { ContentMarker } from './contentSignature.js';
import type {
  ExtensionContentSummary,
  HooksSummary,
  McpServerSummary,
} from './extensionContentSummary.js';

const mockReadline = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  createInterface: vi.fn().mockReturnValue({
    question: vi.fn(),
    close: vi.fn(),
  }),
}));

const mockReaddir = vi.hoisted(() => vi.fn());
const originalReaddir = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  current: null as typeof fs.readdir | null,
}));

// Mocking readline for non-interactive prompts
vi.mock('node:readline', () => ({
  default: mockReadline,
  createInterface: mockReadline.createInterface,
}));

vi.mock('node:fs/promises', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('node:fs/promises')>();
  originalReaddir.current = actual.readdir;
  return {
    ...actual,
    readdir: mockReaddir,
  };
});

vi.mock('@google/gemini-cli-core', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual =
    await importOriginal<typeof import('@google/gemini-cli-core')>();
  return {
    ...actual,
    debugLogger: {
      log: vi.fn(),
    },
  };
});

async function expectConsentSnapshot(consentString: string) {
  const renderResult = await render(
    React.createElement(Text, null, consentString),
  );
  await expect(renderResult).toMatchSvgSnapshot();
}

/**
 * Normalizes a consent string for snapshot testing by:
 * 1. Replacing the dynamic temp directory path with a static placeholder.
 * 2. Converting Windows backslashes to forward slashes for platform-agnosticism.
 */
function normalizePathsForSnapshot(str: string, tempDir: string): string {
  return str.replaceAll(tempDir, '/mock/temp/dir').replaceAll('\\', '/');
}

describe('consent', () => {
  let tempDir: string;
  const originalStdinIsTTY = process.stdin.isTTY;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    Object.defineProperty(process.stdin, 'isTTY', {
      value: true,
      configurable: true,
    });
    if (originalReaddir.current) {
      // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
      mockReaddir.mockImplementation(originalReaddir.current as any);
    }
    tempDir = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'consent-test-'));
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    Object.defineProperty(process.stdin, 'isTTY', {
      value: originalStdinIsTTY,
      configurable: true,
    });
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
    if (tempDir) {
      await fs.rm(tempDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    }
    cleanup();
  });

  describe('requestConsentNonInteractive', () => {
    it.each([
      { input: 'y', expected: true },
      { input: 'Y', expected: true },
      { input: '', expected: false },
      { input: 'n', expected: false },
      { input: 'N', expected: false },
      { input: 'yes', expected: true },
    ])(
      'should return $expected for input "$input"',
      async ({ input, expected }) => {
        const questionMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation((_, callback) => {
          callback(input);
        });
        mockReadline.createInterface.mockReturnValue({
          question: questionMock,
          close: vi.fn(),
        });

        const consent = await requestConsentNonInteractive('Test consent');
        expect(debugLogger.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Test consent');
        expect(questionMock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
          'Do you want to continue? [y/N]: ',
          expect.any(Function),
        );
        expect(consent).toBe(expected);
      },
    );

    it('should fail closed and return false when readline closes on EOF without an answer', async () => {
      let closeHandler: (() => void) | undefined;
      const questionMock = vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => {
        closeHandler?.();
      });
      mockReadline.createInterface.mockReturnValue({
        question: questionMock,
        on: vi.fn().mockImplementation((event: string, cb: () => void) => {
          if (event === 'close') {
            closeHandler = cb;
          }
        }),
        close: vi.fn(),
      });

      const consent = await requestConsentNonInteractive('Test consent');
      expect(debugLogger.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Test consent');
      expect(consent).toBe(false);
    });

    it('should ask concurrent consent requests one at a time', async () => {
      const answers: Array<(answer: string) => void> = [];
      const questionMock = vi
        .fn()
        .mockImplementation(
          (_prompt: string, callback: (answer: string) => void) => {
            answers.push(callback);
          },
        );
      mockReadline.createInterface.mockReturnValue({
        question: questionMock,
        close: vi.fn(),
      });

      const first = requestConsentNonInteractive('First consent');
      const second = requestConsentNonInteractive('Second consent');

      await vi.waitFor(() => expect(questionMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1));
      expect(debugLogger.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith('First consent');
      expect(debugLogger.log).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith('Second consent');

      answers[0]('y');
      await expect(first).resolves.toBe(true);
      await vi.waitFor(() => expect(questionMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2));
      expect(debugLogger.log).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Second consent');

      answers[1]('n');
      await expect(second).resolves.toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('requestConsentInteractive', () => {
    it.each([
      { confirmed: true, expected: true },
      { confirmed: false, expected: false },
    ])(
      'should resolve with $expected when user confirms with $confirmed',
      async ({ confirmed, expected }) => {
        const addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest = vi
          .fn()
          .mockImplementation((request: ConfirmationRequest) => {
            request.onConfirm(confirmed);
          });

        const consent = await requestConsentInteractive(
          'Test consent',
          addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest,
        );

        expect(addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
          prompt: 'Test consent\n\nDo you want to continue?',
          onConfirm: expect.any(Function),
        });
        expect(consent).toBe(expected);
      },
    );

    it('should clear the active confirmation request before resolving', async () => {
      const clearConfirmationRequest = vi.fn();
      const steps: string[] = [];
      const addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest = vi
        .fn()
        .mockImplementation((request: ConfirmationRequest) => {
          steps.push('prompted');
          request.onConfirm(true);
          steps.push('confirmed');
        });

      const consentPromise = requestConsentInteractive(
        'Test consent',
        addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest,
        () => {
          steps.push('cleared');
          clearConfirmationRequest();
        },
      ).then((consent) => {
        steps.push('resolved');
        return consent;
      });

      expect(clearConfirmationRequest).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      expect(steps).toEqual(['prompted', 'cleared', 'confirmed']);
      await expect(consentPromise).resolves.toBe(true);
      expect(steps).toEqual(['prompted', 'cleared', 'confirmed', 'resolved']);
    });

    it('passes defaultToNo to the confirmation request when asked to', async () => {
      const addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest = vi
        .fn()
        .mockImplementation((request: ConfirmationRequest) => {
          request.onConfirm(false);
        });

      await requestConsentInteractive(
        'Install it?',
        addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest,
        undefined,
        { defaultToNo: true },
      );

      expect(addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        prompt: 'Install it?\n\nDo you want to continue?',
        defaultToNo: true,
        onConfirm: expect.any(Function),
      });
    });
  });

  describe('maybeRequestConsentOrFail', () => {
    const baseConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
      name: 'test-ext',
      version: '1.0.0',
    };

    it('should request consent if there is no previous config', async () => {
      const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
      await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
        baseConfig,
        requestConsent,
        false,
        undefined,
      );
      expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    });

    it('should not request consent if configs are identical', async () => {
      const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
      await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
        baseConfig,
        requestConsent,
        false,
        baseConfig,
        false,
      );
      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('should throw an error if consent is denied', async () => {
      const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(false);
      await expect(
        maybeRequestConsentOrFail(baseConfig, requestConsent, false, undefined),
      ).rejects.toThrow('Installation cancelled for "test-ext".');
    });

    it('should request consent when transitioning from a non-linked extension to a linked extension', async () => {
      const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
      await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
        baseConfig,
        requestConsent,
        false,
        baseConfig,
        false,
        [],
        [],
        false,
        '/canonical/linked/path',
        undefined,
      );
      expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    });

    it('should request consent when linkedSourcePath changes between updates', async () => {
      const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
      await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
        baseConfig,
        requestConsent,
        false,
        baseConfig,
        false,
        [],
        [],
        false,
        '/new/canonical/linked/path',
        '/old/canonical/linked/path',
      );
      expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    });

    it('should not request consent when linkedSourcePath and previousLinkedSourcePath are identical', async () => {
      const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
      await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
        baseConfig,
        requestConsent,
        false,
        baseConfig,
        false,
        [],
        [],
        false,
        '/same/canonical/linked/path',
        '/same/canonical/linked/path',
      );
      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    describe('consent string generation', () => {
      it('should generate a consent string with all fields', async () => {
        const config: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: {
            server1: { command: 'npm', args: ['start'] },
            server2: { httpUrl: 'https://remote.com' },
          },
          contextFileName: 'my-context.md',
          excludeTools: ['tool1', 'tool2'],
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          config,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          undefined,
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        const consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;
        await expectConsentSnapshot(consentString);
      });

      it('should sort environment variables alphabetically and handle undefined envValue', async () => {
        const config: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: {
            server1: {
              command: 'node',
              args: ['server.js'],
              env: {
                VAR_B: 'b',
                VAR_A: 'a',
                VAR_C: undefined as unknown as string,
              },
            },
          },
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          config,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          undefined,
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        const consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - VAR_A: a');
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - VAR_B: b');
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - VAR_C: ');

        const posA = consentString.indexOf('      - VAR_A: a');
        const posB = consentString.indexOf('      - VAR_B: b');
        const posC = consentString.indexOf('      - VAR_C: ');
        expect(posA).toBeLessThan(posB);
        expect(posB).toBeLessThan(posC);
      });

      it('should mask sensitive environment variables, headers, and OAuth parameters', async () => {
        const config: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: {
            server1: {
              command: 'node',
              args: ['server.js'],
              env: {
                SAFE_VAR: 'safe-value',
                SUPER_TOKEN: 'secret-token-123',
                DB_PASSWORD: 'my-password',
              },
              headers: {
                'X-API-Key': 'some-api-key',
                Authorization: 'Bearer 12345',
                'Content-Type': 'application/json',
              },
              oauth: {
                clientId: 'my-client-id',
                clientSecret: 'secret-oauth-value',
              },
            },
          },
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          config,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          undefined,
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        const consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;

        // Assert sensitive env values are masked
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - SAFE_VAR: safe-value');
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - SUPER_TOKEN: ********');
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - DB_PASSWORD: ********');

        // Assert sensitive headers are masked
        expect(consentString).toContain(
          '      - Content-Type: application/json',
        );
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - Authorization: ********');
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - X-API-Key: ********');

        // Assert sensitive OAuth parameters are masked
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - clientId: my-client-id');
        expect(consentString).toContain('      - clientSecret: ********');
      });

      it('should request consent if mcpServers change', async () => {
        const prevConfig: ExtensionConfig = { ...baseConfig };
        const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: { server1: { command: 'npm', args: ['start'] } },
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          newConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          prevConfig,
          false,
        );
        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      });

      it('should request consent if mcpServer env changes', async () => {
        const prevConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: {
            server1: { command: 'node', args: ['server.js'] },
          },
        };
        const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: {
            server1: {
              command: 'node',
              args: ['server.js'],
              env: { NODE_OPTIONS: '--require=./payload.js' },
            },
          },
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          newConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          prevConfig,
          false,
        );
        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      });

      it('should request consent if contextFileName changes', async () => {
        const prevConfig: ExtensionConfig = { ...baseConfig };
        const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          contextFileName: 'new-context.md',
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          newConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          prevConfig,
          false,
        );
        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      });

      it('should request consent if excludeTools changes', async () => {
        const prevConfig: ExtensionConfig = { ...baseConfig };
        const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          excludeTools: ['new-tool'],
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          newConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          prevConfig,
          false,
        );
        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      });

      it('should include warning when hooks are present', async () => {
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          baseConfig,
          requestConsent,
          true,
          undefined,
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        const consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;
        await expectConsentSnapshot(consentString);
      });

      it('should request consent if hooks status changes', async () => {
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          baseConfig,
          requestConsent,
          true,
          baseConfig,
          false,
        );
        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      });

      it('should request consent if extension is migrated', async () => {
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          baseConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          { ...baseConfig, name: 'old-ext' },
          false,
          [],
          [],
          true,
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        let consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;
        consentString = normalizePathsForSnapshot(consentString, tempDir);
        await expectConsentSnapshot(consentString);
      });

      it('should request consent if skills change', async () => {
        const skill1Dir = path.join(tempDir, 'skill1');
        const skill2Dir = path.join(tempDir, 'skill2');
        await fs.mkdir(skill1Dir, { recursive: true });
        await fs.mkdir(skill2Dir, { recursive: true });
        await fs.writeFile(path.join(skill1Dir, 'SKILL.md'), 'body1');
        await fs.writeFile(path.join(skill1Dir, 'extra.txt'), 'extra');
        await fs.writeFile(path.join(skill2Dir, 'SKILL.md'), 'body2');

        const skill1: SkillDefinition = {
          name: 'skill1',
          description: 'desc1',
          location: path.join(skill1Dir, 'SKILL.md'),
          body: 'body1',
        };
        const skill2: SkillDefinition = {
          name: 'skill2',
          description: 'desc2',
          location: path.join(skill2Dir, 'SKILL.md'),
          body: 'body2',
        };

        const config: ExtensionConfig = {
          ...baseConfig,
          mcpServers: {
            server1: { command: 'npm', args: ['start'] },
            server2: { httpUrl: 'https://remote.com' },
          },
          contextFileName: 'my-context.md',
          excludeTools: ['tool1', 'tool2'],
        };
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          config,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          undefined,
          false,
          [skill1, skill2],
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        let consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;
        consentString = normalizePathsForSnapshot(consentString, tempDir);
        await expectConsentSnapshot(consentString);
      });

      it('should show a warning if the skill directory cannot be read', async () => {
        const lockedDir = path.join(tempDir, 'locked');
        await fs.mkdir(lockedDir, { recursive: true });

        const skill: SkillDefinition = {
          name: 'locked-skill',
          description: 'A skill in a locked dir',
          location: path.join(lockedDir, 'SKILL.md'),
          body: 'body',
        };

        // Mock readdir to simulate a permission error.
        // We do this instead of using fs.mkdir(..., { mode: 0o000 }) because
        // directory permissions work differently on Windows and 0o000 doesn't
        // effectively block access there, leading to test failures in Windows CI.
        mockReaddir.mockRejectedValueOnce(
          new Error('EACCES: permission denied, scandir'),
        );

        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          baseConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          undefined,
          false,
          [skill],
        );

        expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
        let consentString = requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0] as string;
        consentString = normalizePathsForSnapshot(consentString, tempDir);
        await expectConsentSnapshot(consentString);
      });
    });

    describe('content summaries', () => {
      const signature = 'a'.repeat(64);
      const otherSignature = 'b'.repeat(64);

      function hooksSummary(
        overrides: Partial<HooksSummary> = {},
      ): HooksSummary {
        return {
          hooks: [{ eventName: 'SessionStart', command: 'echo v1', env: [] }],
          files: [],
          referencedPaths: [],
          signature,
          ...overrides,
        };
      }

      async function consentTextFor(
        current: ExtensionContentSummary,
        previous?: ExtensionContentSummary,
      ): Promise<string | undefined> {
        const requestConsent = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true);
        await maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
          baseConfig,
          requestConsent,
          false,
          previous ? baseConfig : undefined,
          false,
          [],
          [],
          false,
          undefined,
          undefined,
          { current, previous },
        );
        return requestConsent.mock.calls[0]?.[0] as string | undefined;
      }

      it('lists each hook with its details, the paths it uses, and a signature', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor({
          hooks: hooksSummary({
            hooks: [
              {
                eventName: 'BeforeTool',
                matcher: 'run_shell_command',
                command: 'node ${extensionPath}/scripts/check.js',
                env: [
                  ['API_TOKEN', 'abc'],
                  ['LOG_LEVEL', 'debug'],
                ],
              },
              {
                eventName: 'SessionStart',
                name: 'greeting',
                command: 'echo `id`',
                env: [],
              },
              { eventName: 'SessionEnd', type: 'runtime', env: [] },
            ],
            referencedPaths: [
              { path: '.', marker: ContentMarker.Root, signature },
              {
                path: '../shared.sh',
                marker: ContentMarker.Outside,
                signature,
              },
              { path: 'scripts/check.js', signature },
              {
                path: 'scripts/gone.js',
                marker: ContentMarker.Missing,
                signature,
              },
            ],
          }),
        });

        expect(text).toContain(
          [
            '⚠️  This extension contains Hooks which can automatically execute commands:',
            '  * BeforeTool (matcher: `run_shell_command`): `node ${extensionPath}/scripts/check.js`',
            '      Environment variables:',
            '        - API_TOKEN: ********',
            '        - LOG_LEVEL: `debug`',
            '  * SessionStart (name: `greeting`): `` echo `id` ``',
            '  * SessionEnd: no command, type `runtime`',
            '  Files used by hooks: `.` (the extension folder), `../shared.sh` (outside the extension folder), `scripts/check.js`, `scripts/gone.js` (not found)',
            `  Hooks signature: ${signature}`,
          ].join('\n'),
        );
      });

      it('escapes control characters in hook values', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor({
          hooks: hooksSummary({
            hooks: [
              {
                eventName: 'Session\u202eStart',
                command: 'echo hi\n\u001b[2J\r',
                env: [['MODE', 'a\tb']],
              },
            ],
          }),
        });

        expect(text).toContain(
          '  * Session\\u202eStart: `echo hi\\n\\u001b[2J\\r`',
        );
        expect(text).toContain('        - MODE: `a\\tb`');
      });

      it('says when hooks.json is not a valid hooks file', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor({
          hooks: hooksSummary({ hooks: undefined }),
        });

        expect(text).toContain(
          "  * `hooks/hooks.json` isn't a valid hooks file, so its hooks can't be listed.",
        );
        expect(text).toContain(`  Hooks signature: ${signature}`);
      });

      it('prints no hooks section when the summary has no hooks', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor({});

        expect(text).not.toContain('Hooks');
      });

      it('does not ask for consent when both summaries match', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor(
          { hooks: hooksSummary() },
          { hooks: hooksSummary() },
        );

        expect(text).toBeUndefined();
      });

      it('asks for consent when only the hooks signature changes', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor(
          { hooks: hooksSummary({ signature: otherSignature }) },
          { hooks: hooksSummary() },
        );

        expect(text).toContain(`  Hooks signature: ${otherSignature}`);
      });

      it('shows the changes after the warnings without comparing them', async () => {
        const current = {
          hooks: hooksSummary({
            hooks: [{ eventName: 'SessionStart', command: 'echo v2', env: [] }],
            signature: otherSignature,
          }),
        };
        const installText = await consentTextFor(current);

        const updateText = await consentTextFor(current, {
          hooks: hooksSummary(),
        });

        expect(updateText).toBe(
          [
            installText,
            '',
            'Changes since the installed version:',
            '  * Hooks: new or changed `SessionStart: echo v2`',
          ].join('\n'),
        );
      });

      it('names the files and referenced paths that were added, changed, or removed', async () => {
        const text = await consentTextFor(
          {
            hooks: hooksSummary({
              files: [
                { path: 'hooks/a.sh', type: 'file', value: otherSignature },
                { path: 'hooks/new.sh', type: 'file', value: signature },
              ],
              referencedPaths: [{ path: 'scripts/run.js', signature }],
              signature: otherSignature,
            }),
          },
          {

export const INSTALL_WARNING_MESSAGE = chalk.yellow(
  'The extension you are about to install may have been created by a third-party developer and sourced from a public repository. Google does not vet, endorse, or guarantee the functionality or security of extensions. Please carefully inspect any extension and its source code before installing to understand the permissions it requires and the actions it may perform.',

export const LINK_WARNING_MESSAGE = chalk.yellow(
  '⚠️  Warning: Linking creates a live symbolic link to the target directory. Any future changes made to code, MCP servers, hooks, or prompts inside that directory will take effect automatically upon CLI startup without further warnings.',
);

export const SKILLS_WARNING_MESSAGE = chalk.yellow(
  "Agent skills inject specialized instructions and domain-specific knowledge into the agent's system prompt. This can change how the agent interprets your requests and interacts with your environment. Review the skill definitions at the location(s) provided below to ensure they meet your security standards.",
);

/**
 * Builds a consent string for installing agent skills.
 */
export async function skillsConsentString(
  skills: SkillDefinition[],
  source: string,
  targetDir?: string,
  isLink = false,
): Promise<string> {
  const action = isLink ? 'Linking' : 'Installing';
  const output: string[] = [];
  output.push(`${action} agent skill(s) from "${source}".`);
  output.push(
    `\nThe following agent skill(s) will be ${action.toLowerCase()}:\n`,
  );
  output.push(...(await renderSkillsList(skills)));

  if (targetDir) {
    const destLabel = isLink ? 'Link' : 'Install';
    output.push(`${destLabel} Destination: ${targetDir}`);
  }
  output.push('\n' + SKILLS_WARNING_MESSAGE);

  return output.join('\n');
}

/**
 * Non-interactive prompts share stdin, so they run one at a time: each one
 * prints its description only after the previous one has its answer. The
 * queue is module-scoped on purpose: every caller reads the same process
 * stdin, so a queue per caller or per ExtensionManager wouldn't keep their
 * prompts apart. It only holds the promise of the latest prompt.
 */
let nonInteractiveConsentQueue: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve();

/**
 * Requests consent from the user to perform an action, by reading a Y/n
 * character from stdin.
 *
 * This should not be called from interactive mode as it will break the CLI.
 *
 * @param consentDescription The description of the thing they will be consenting to.
 * @returns boolean, whether they consented or not.
 */
export async function requestConsentNonInteractive(
  consentDescription: string,
): Promise<boolean> {
  const ask = async () => {
    debugLogger.log(consentDescription);
    return promptForConsentNonInteractive(
      'Do you want to continue? [y/N]: ',
      false,
    );
  };
  const result = nonInteractiveConsentQueue.then(ask);
  nonInteractiveConsentQueue = result.catch(() => undefined);
  return result;
}

/**
 * Requests consent from the user to perform an action, in interactive mode.
 *
 * This should not be called from non-interactive mode as it will not work.
 *
 * @param consentDescription The description of the thing they will be consenting to.
 * @param addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest A function to actually add a prompt to the UI.
 * @param options.defaultToNo Selects "No" first in the dialog, so pressing
 *   Enter declines. Extension installs and updates use it.
 * @returns boolean, whether they consented or not.
 */
export async function requestConsentInteractive(
  consentDescription: string,
  addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest: (value: ConfirmationRequest) => void,
  clearConfirmationRequest?: () => void,
  options: { defaultToNo?: boolean } = {},
): Promise<boolean> {
  return promptForConsentInteractive(
    consentDescription + '\n\nDo you want to continue?',
    addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest,
    clearConfirmationRequest,
    options.defaultToNo ?? false,
  );
}

/**
 * Asks users a prompt and awaits for a y/n response on stdin.
 *
 * This should not be called from interactive mode as it will break the CLI.
 *
 * @param prompt A yes/no prompt to ask the user
 * @param defaultValue Whether to resolve as true or false on enter.
 * @returns Whether or not the user answers 'y' (yes).
 */
export async function promptForConsentNonInteractive(
  prompt: string,
  defaultValue = false,
): Promise<boolean> {
  const readline = await import('node:readline');
  const rl = readline.createInterface({
    input: process.stdin,
    output: process.stdout,
  });

  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    let settled = false;
    const finish = (value: boolean) => {
      if (settled) {
        return;
      }
      settled = true;
      rl.close();
      resolve(value);
    };

    rl.on?.('close', () => {
      finish(false);
    });

    rl.question(prompt, (answer) => {
      const trimmedAnswer = answer.trim().toLowerCase();
      if (trimmedAnswer === '') {
        finish(defaultValue);
      } else {
        finish(['y', 'yes'].includes(trimmedAnswer));
      }
    });
  });
}

/**
 * Asks users an interactive yes/no prompt.
 *
 * This should not be called from non-interactive mode as it will break the CLI.
 *
 * @param prompt A markdown prompt to ask the user
 * @param addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest Function to update the UI state with the confirmation request.
 * @param defaultToNo Whether the dialog selects "No" first.
 * @returns Whether or not the user answers yes.
 */
async function promptForConsentInteractive(
  prompt: string,
  addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest: (value: ConfirmationRequest) => void,
  clearConfirmationRequest?: () => void,
  defaultToNo = false,
): Promise<boolean> {
  return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
    addExtensionUpdateConfirmationRequest({
      prompt,
      ...(defaultToNo ? { defaultToNo } : {}),
      onConfirm: (resolvedConfirmed) => {
        clearConfirmationRequest?.();
        setImmediate(() => resolve(resolvedConfirmed));
      },
    });
  });
}

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

/**
 * Helper to generate a deterministic canonical hash of an MCPServerConfig object.
 * Excludes circular or complex fields like extension.
 */
function getMcpServerConfigHash(mcpServer: MCPServerConfig): string {
  const plainMcpServer: Record<string, unknown> = isRecord(mcpServer)
    ? mcpServer
    : {};
  const copy = { ...plainMcpServer };
  delete copy['extension'];

  const canonicalString = JSON.stringify(copy, (key, value) => {
    if (value instanceof RegExp) {
      return value.toString();
    }
    if (isRecord(value)) {
      return Object.keys(value)
        .sort()
        .reduce((result: Record<string, unknown>, k) => {
          result[k] = value[k];
          return result;
        }, {});
    }
    return value as unknown;
  });

  return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(canonicalString).digest('hex');
}

/** Environment variable names whose values the consent text masks. */
const SENSITIVE_ENV_NAME =
  /token|secret|password|passwd|key|auth|credential|creds|private|cert/i;

/** Header names whose values the consent text masks. */
const SENSITIVE_HEADER_NAME = /authorization|key|cookie|token|secret/i;

/** OAuth setting names whose values the consent text masks. */
const SENSITIVE_OAUTH_NAME = /secret|token|password/i;

const HOOKS_HEADING =
  '⚠️  This extension contains Hooks which can automatically execute commands';

const CHANGES_HEADING = 'Changes since the installed version:';

/** Most file lines that the change block lists outside the other sections. */
const MAX_FILE_CHANGE_LINES = 20;

/**
 * Escapes a value, or each value of a list joined with `,` (the way a list
 * prints in a template string), with {@link escapeForDisplay}.
 */
function escapeListForDisplay(value: unknown): string {
  return Array.isArray(value)
    ? value.map((item) => escapeForDisplay(String(item))).join(',')
    : escapeForDisplay(String(value));
}

function formatEnvValue(name: string, value: string): string {
  return SENSITIVE_ENV_NAME.test(name) && value
    ? '********'
    : formatValueForDisplay(value);
}

function formatPathNote(
  label: string,
  marker: ContentMarker | undefined,
): string {
  switch (marker) {
    case undefined:
    case ContentMarker.Directory:
      return label;
    case ContentMarker.Root:
      return `${label} (the extension folder)`;
    case ContentMarker.Outside:
      return `${label} (outside the extension folder)`;
    case ContentMarker.Missing:
      return `${label} (not found)`;
    case ContentMarker.Dangling:
      return `${label} (broken link)`;
    case ContentMarker.Unsupported:
      return `${label} (not a regular file)`;
    default:
      return `${label} (unreadable)`;
  }
}

function formatReferencedPath(reference: ReferencedPath): string {
  return formatPathNote(
    formatValueForDisplay(reference.path),
    reference.marker,
  );
}

function formatEntryPath(entry: ContentEntry): string {
  return formatPathNote(
    formatValueForDisplay(entry.path),
    asContentMarker(entry.value),
  );
}

function formatHook(hook: HookSummary): string {
  const details: string[] = [];
  if (hook.matcher !== undefined) {
    details.push(`matcher: ${formatValueForDisplay(hook.matcher)}`);
  }
  if (hook.name !== undefined) {
    details.push(`name: ${formatValueForDisplay(hook.name)}`);
  }
  const qualifier = details.length > 0 ? ` (${details.join(', ')})` : '';
  const action =
    hook.command !== undefined
      ? formatValueForDisplay(hook.command)
      : `no command, type ${formatValueForDisplay(hook.type ?? '')}`;
  return `${escapeForDisplay(hook.eventName)}${qualifier}: ${action}`;
}

function renderHooksSection(summary: HooksSummary): string[] {
  const output = [`${HOOKS_HEADING}:`];
  if (!summary.hooks) {
    output.push(
      `  * ${formatValueForDisplay('hooks/hooks.json')} isn't a valid hooks file, so its hooks can't be listed.`,
    );
  }
  for (const hook of summary.hooks ?? []) {
    output.push(`  * ${formatHook(hook)}`);
    if (hook.env.length > 0) {
      output.push('      Environment variables:');
      for (const [name, value] of hook.env) {
        output.push(
          `        - ${escapeForDisplay(name)}: ${formatEnvValue(name, value)}`,
        );
      }
    }
  }
  if (summary.referencedPaths.length > 0) {
    output.push(
      `  Files used by hooks: ${summary.referencedPaths.map(formatReferencedPath).join(', ')}`,
    );
  }
  output.push(`  Hooks signature: ${summary.signature}`);
  return output;
}

function renderContextFilesDetails(summary: ContextFilesSummary): string[] {
  const output: string[] = [];
  if (summary.importedPaths.length > 0) {
    output.push(
      `  Imported files: ${summary.importedPaths.map((importedPath) => formatValueForDisplay(importedPath)).join(', ')}`,
    );
  }
  output.push(`  Context files signature: ${summary.signature}`);
  return output;
}

function sortedEntries<T>(
  record: Record<string, T> | undefined,
): Array<[string, T]> {
  return Object.entries(record ?? {}).sort(([a], [b]) =>
    compareCodeUnits(a, b),
  );
}

/**
 * Lists the MCP server of a sub-agent like a manifest MCP server, with values
 * as written, escaped, and in code spans.
 */
function renderAgentMcpServer(name: string, server: MCPServerConfig): string[] {
  const indent = '      ';
  const isLocal = !!server.command;
  const source =
    server.httpUrl ??
    `${server.command || ''}${server.args ? ' ' + server.args.join(' ') : ''}`;
  const output = [
    `${indent}MCP server ${formatValueForDisplay(name)} (${isLocal ? 'local' : 'remote'}): ${formatValueForDisplay(source)}`,
  ];
  if (server.cwd) {
    output.push(
      `${indent}Working directory: ${formatValueForDisplay(server.cwd)}`,
    );
  }
  const env = sortedEntries(server.env);
  if (env.length > 0) {
    output.push(`${indent}Environment variables:`);
    for (const [envName, value] of env) {
      output.push(
        `${indent}  - ${escapeForDisplay(envName)}: ${formatEnvValue(envName, value ?? '')}`,
      );
    }
  }
  const headers = sortedEntries(server.headers);
  if (headers.length > 0) {
    output.push(`${indent}Headers:`);
    for (const [headerName, value] of headers) {
      const displayValue =
        SENSITIVE_HEADER_NAME.test(headerName) && value
          ? '********'
          : formatValueForDisplay(value ?? '');
      output.push(
        `${indent}  - ${escapeForDisplay(headerName)}: ${displayValue}`,
      );
    }
  }
  if (server.url) {
    output.push(`${indent}URL: ${formatValueForDisplay(server.url)}`);
  }
  if (server.tcp) {
    output.push(`${indent}TCP: ${formatValueForDisplay(server.tcp)}`);
  }
  if (server.type) {
    output.push(`${indent}Type: ${formatValueForDisplay(server.type)}`);
  }
  if (server.timeout !== undefined) {
    output.push(`${indent}Timeout: ${escapeListForDisplay(server.timeout)}`);
  }
  if (server.trust !== undefined) {
    output.push(`${indent}Trust: ${escapeListForDisplay(server.trust)}`);
  }
  if (server.description) {
    output.push(
      `${indent}Description: ${formatValueForDisplay(server.description)}`,
    );
  }
  for (const [label, tools] of [
    ['Include tools', server.includeTools],
    ['Exclude tools', server.excludeTools],
  ] as const) {
    if (tools && tools.length > 0) {
      output.push(
        `${indent}${label}: ${tools.map((tool) => formatValueForDisplay(tool)).join(', ')}`,
      );
    }
  }
  if (server.authProviderType) {
    output.push(
      `${indent}Auth Provider Type: ${formatValueForDisplay(server.authProviderType)}`,
    );
  }
  if (server.oauth) {
    output.push(`${indent}OAuth Configuration:`);
    for (const [key, value] of sortedEntries<unknown>({ ...server.oauth })) {
      const text = Array.isArray(value)
        ? value.join(', ')
        : String(value ?? '');
      const displayValue =
        SENSITIVE_OAUTH_NAME.test(key) && text
          ? '********'
          : formatValueForDisplay(text);
      output.push(`${indent}  - ${escapeForDisplay(key)}: ${displayValue}`);
    }
  }
  return output;
}

function renderAgentsSection(summary: AgentsSummary): string[] {
  const output = ['This extension will add the following sub-agents:'];
  for (const agent of summary.agents) {
    if (agent.name === undefined) {
      output.push(
        `  * ${formatValueForDisplay(agent.path)} isn't a valid sub-agent file.`,
      );
      continue;
    }
    output.push(
      `  * ${formatValueForDisplay(agent.name)} (${formatValueForDisplay(agent.path)})`,
    );
    if (agent.agentCardUrl !== undefined) {
      output.push(
        `      Agent card URL: ${formatValueForDisplay(agent.agentCardUrl)}`,
      );
    }
    for (const [name, server] of agent.mcpServers) {
      output.push(...renderAgentMcpServer(name, server));
    }
  }
  for (const entry of summary.files) {
    // The agents folder itself, when it's a link that can't be followed.
    if (entry.path === 'agents' && entry.value !== ContentMarker.Directory) {
      output.push(`  * ${formatEntryPath(entry)}`);
    }
  }
  if (summary.referencedPaths.length > 0) {
    output.push(
      `  Files used by MCP servers: ${summary.referencedPaths.map(formatReferencedPath).join(', ')}`,
    );
  }
  output.push(`  Agents signature: ${summary.signature}`);
  return output;
}

function renderFilesSection(
  heading: string,
  signatureLabel: string,
  summary: FilesSummary,
): string[] {
  return [
    heading,
    ...summary.files
      .filter((entry) => entry.value !== ContentMarker.Directory)
      .map((entry) => `  * ${formatEntryPath(entry)}`),
    `  ${signatureLabel}: ${summary.signature}`,
  ];
}

/**
 * Lists skills like `renderSkillsList`, with paths relative to the extension
 * folder, escaped values, the links under `skills/` that leave the folder or
 * are broken, and a signature line.
 */
function renderSkillSummaries(summary: SkillsSummary): string[] {
  const output: string[] = [];
  for (const skill of summary.skills) {
    output.push(
      `  * ${chalk.bold(escapeForDisplay(skill.name))}: ${escapeForDisplay(skill.description)}`,
    );
    const fileCountStr =
      skill.itemCount !== undefined
        ? ` (${skill.itemCount} items in directory)`
        : ` ${chalk.red('⚠️ (Could not count items in directory)')}`;
    output.push(
      chalk.dim(
        `    (Source: ${escapeForDisplay(skill.location)})${fileCountStr}`,
      ),
    );
    output.push('');
  }
  for (const entry of summary.files) {
    if (isUnresolvedLink(entry)) {
      output.push(`  * ${formatEntryPath(entry)}`, '');
    }
  }
  output.push(`  Skills signature: ${summary.signature}`);
  return output;
}

/** The settings of a loaded config, for a consent text without a summary. */
function loadedSettings(config: ExtensionConfig): SettingSummary[] {
  return (config.settings ?? []).map((setting) => ({
    name: String(setting.name ?? ''),
    envVar: String(setting.envVar ?? ''),
    sensitive: setting.sensitive === true,
  }));
}

function renderSettings(settings: readonly SettingSummary[]): string[] {
  return [
    'This extension will receive these settings in environment variables:',
    ...settings.map(
      (setting) =>
        `  * ${formatValueForDisplay(setting.name)}: ${formatValueForDisplay(setting.envVar)}${setting.sensitive ? ' (sensitive)' : ''}`,
    ),
  ];
}

/** Hashes per skill folder, plus files under `skills/` outside any skill. */
function skillHashes(summary: SkillsSummary | undefined): Map<string, string> {
  const hashes = new Map<string, string>();
  const folders: string[] = [];
  for (const skill of summary?.skills ?? []) {
    const folder = path.posix.dirname(skill.location);
    folders.push(folder);
    hashes.set(folder, skill.signature);
  }
  for (const entry of summary?.files ?? []) {
    const inSkillFolder = folders.some(
      (folder) => entry.path === folder || entry.path.startsWith(`${folder}/`),
    );
    if (!inSkillFolder) {
      hashes.set(entry.path, `${entry.type}\0${entry.value}`);
    }
  }
  return hashes;
}

/** Lists the items that were added, changed, or removed, keyed by label. */
function describeItemChanges(
  section: string,
  previous: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
  current: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
): string[] {
  const labels = [...new Set([...previous.keys(), ...current.keys()])].sort(
    compareCodeUnits,
  );
  const lines: string[] = [];
  for (const label of labels) {
    const before = previous.get(label);
    const after = current.get(label);
    if (before === after) {
      continue;
    }
    let change = 'changed';
    if (before === undefined) {
      change = 'added';
    } else if (after === undefined) {
      change = 'removed';
    }
    lines.push(`  * ${section}: ${formatValueForDisplay(label)} ${change}`);
  }
  return lines;
}

function fileHashes(
  entries: readonly ContentEntry[],
  excludedPath?: string,
): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    entries
      .filter((entry) => entry.path !== excludedPath)
      .map((entry) => [entry.path, `${entry.type}\0${entry.value}`]),
  );
}

function referenceHashes(
  references: readonly ReferencedPath[],
): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    references.map((reference) => [reference.path, reference.signature]),
  );
}

function mcpServerHashes(
  servers: ReadonlyArray<[string, McpServerSummary]> | undefined,
): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    (servers ?? []).map(([name, server]) => [
      name,
      getMcpServerConfigHash(escapeAnsiCtrlCodes(server.config)),
    ]),
  );
}

function mcpReferenceHashes(
  servers: ReadonlyArray<[string, McpServerSummary]> | undefined,
): Map<string, string> {
  return referenceHashes(
    (servers ?? []).flatMap(([, server]) => server.referencedPaths),
  );
}

function settingHashes(
  settings: readonly SettingSummary[] | undefined,
): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    (settings ?? []).map((setting) => [
      setting.name,
      JSON.stringify([setting.envVar, setting.sensitive]),
    ]),
  );
}

function planDirectoryHashes(
  planDirectory: string | undefined,
): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(planDirectory !== undefined ? [[planDirectory, '']] : []);
}

/**
 * Paths that the other lines of the change block cover: the files of each
 * section, and the paths inside the folder that hooks and MCP servers
 * reference. The entry of a folder link doesn't count, only the files listed
 * under it.
 */
function coveredPaths(summary: ExtensionContentSummary): string[] {
  const references = [
    ...(summary.hooks?.referencedPaths ?? []),
    ...(summary.agents?.referencedPaths ?? []),
    ...(summary.mcpServers ?? []).flatMap(
      ([, server]) => server.referencedPaths,
    ),
  ];
  return [
    ...[
      summary.hooks,
      summary.contextFiles,
      summary.skills,
      summary.agents,
      summary.commands,
      summary.policies,
    ].flatMap((section) =>
      (section?.files ?? [])
        .filter((entry) => entry.value !== ContentMarker.Directory)
        .map((entry) => entry.path),
    ),
    ...references
      .filter((reference) => reference.marker === undefined)
      .map((reference) => reference.path),
  ];
}

/**
 * Names the files that changed and that no other line of the change block
 * covers, up to {@link MAX_FILE_CHANGE_LINES} lines.
 */
function describeOtherFileChanges(
  previous: ExtensionContentSummary,
  current: ExtensionContentSummary,
): string[] {
  const covered = [...coveredPaths(previous), ...coveredPaths(current)];
  const otherFiles = (summary: ExtensionContentSummary) =>
    new Map(
      [...fileHashes(summary.extensionFiles?.files ?? [])].filter(
        ([filePath]) =>
          !covered.some(
            (coveredPath) =>
              filePath === coveredPath ||
              filePath.startsWith(`${coveredPath}/`),
          ),
      ),
    );
  const lines = describeItemChanges(
    'Files',
    otherFiles(previous),
    otherFiles(current),
  );
  if (lines.length <= MAX_FILE_CHANGE_LINES) {
    return lines;
  }
  return [
    ...lines.slice(0, MAX_FILE_CHANGE_LINES),
    `  * Files: ${lines.length - MAX_FILE_CHANGE_LINES} more added, changed, or removed`,
  ];
}

function hookKey(hook: HookSummary): string {
  return JSON.stringify([
    hook.eventName,
    hook.matcher,
    hook.name,
    hook.command,
    hook.type,
    hook.env,
  ]);
}

function hookLabel(hook: HookSummary): string {
  const matcher =
    hook.matcher !== undefined ? ` (matcher: ${hook.matcher})` : '';
  return `${hook.eventName}${matcher}: ${hook.command ?? hook.type ?? ''}`;
}

function describeHookChanges(
  previous: HooksSummary | undefined,
  current: HooksSummary | undefined,
): string[] {
  const previousHooks = new Set((previous?.hooks ?? []).map(hookKey));
  const hookLines = (current?.hooks ?? [])
    .filter((hook) => !previousHooks.has(hookKey(hook)))
    .map(
      (hook) =>
        `  * Hooks: new or changed ${formatValueForDisplay(hookLabel(hook))}`,
    );
  // When hooks changed, they already describe the change to hooks.json.
  const excludedPath = hookLines.length > 0 ? 'hooks/hooks.json' : undefined;
  return [
    ...hookLines,
    ...describeItemChanges(
      'Hooks',
      fileHashes(previous?.files ?? [], excludedPath),
      fileHashes(current?.files ?? [], excludedPath),
    ),
    ...describeItemChanges(
      'Hooks',
      referenceHashes(previous?.referencedPaths ?? []),
      referenceHashes(current?.referencedPaths ?? []),
    ),
  ];
}

/**
 * Describes what changed between the installed and the new content of an
 * extension, for the block shown above the consent question.
 */
function describeContentChanges(
  previous: ExtensionContentSummary,
  current: ExtensionContentSummary,
): string[] {
  return [
    ...new Set([
      ...describeHookChanges(previous.hooks, current.hooks),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Context files',
        fileHashes(previous.contextFiles?.files ?? []),
        fileHashes(current.contextFiles?.files ?? []),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Skills',
        skillHashes(previous.skills),
        skillHashes(current.skills),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Sub-agents',
        fileHashes(previous.agents?.files ?? []),
        fileHashes(current.agents?.files ?? []),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Sub-agents',
        referenceHashes(previous.agents?.referencedPaths ?? []),
        referenceHashes(current.agents?.referencedPaths ?? []),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Custom commands',
        fileHashes(previous.commands?.files ?? []),
        fileHashes(current.commands?.files ?? []),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Policies',
        fileHashes(previous.policies?.files ?? []),
        fileHashes(current.policies?.files ?? []),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'MCP servers',
        mcpServerHashes(previous.mcpServers),
        mcpServerHashes(current.mcpServers),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'MCP servers',
        mcpReferenceHashes(previous.mcpServers),
        mcpReferenceHashes(current.mcpServers),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Settings',
        settingHashes(previous.settings),
        settingHashes(current.settings),
      ),
      ...describeItemChanges(
        'Plan directory',
        planDirectoryHashes(previous.planDirectory),
        planDirectoryHashes(current.planDirectory),
      ),
      ...describeOtherFileChanges(previous, current),
    ]),
  ];
}

/**
 * Builds a consent string for installing an extension based on it's
 * extensionConfig.
 */
async function extensionConsentString(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  hasHooks: boolean,
  skills: SkillDefinition[] = [],
  previousName?: string,
  wasMigrated?: boolean,
  linkedSourcePath?: string,
  contentSummary?: ExtensionContentSummary,
): Promise<string> {
  const sanitizedConfig = escapeAnsiCtrlCodes(extensionConfig);
  const sanitizedLinkedPath = linkedSourcePath
    ? escapeAnsiCtrlCodes(linkedSourcePath)
    : undefined;
  const output: string[] = [];
  const mcpServerEntries = Object.entries(sanitizedConfig.mcpServers || {});
  // With a summary, MCP servers show their values as written in the manifest.
  const rawMcpServers = contentSummary?.mcpServers;
  const mcpServers = rawMcpServers
    ? rawMcpServers.map(([name, server]): [string, MCPServerConfig] => [
        name,
        escapeAnsiCtrlCodes(server.config),
      ])
    : mcpServerEntries;
  const mcpServerFiles = new Map(rawMcpServers ?? []);

  if (wasMigrated) {
    if (previousName && previousName !== sanitizedConfig.name) {
      output.push(
        `Migrating extension "${previousName}" to a new repository, renaming to "${sanitizedConfig.name}", and installing updates.`,
      );
    } else {
      output.push(
        `Migrating extension "${sanitizedConfig.name}" to a new repository and installing updates.`,
      );
    }
  } else if (previousName && previousName !== sanitizedConfig.name) {
    output.push(
      `Renaming extension "${previousName}" to "${sanitizedConfig.name}" and installing updates.`,
    );
  } else if (sanitizedLinkedPath) {
    output.push(
      `Linking extension "${sanitizedConfig.name}" from canonical path "${sanitizedLinkedPath}".`,
    );
  } else {
    output.push(`Installing extension "${sanitizedConfig.name}".`);
  }

  if (mcpServers.length) {
    output.push('This extension will run the following MCP servers:');
    for (const [key, mcpServer] of mcpServers) {
      const isLocal = !!mcpServer.command;
      const source =
        mcpServer.httpUrl ??
        `${mcpServer.command || ''}${mcpServer.args ? ' ' + mcpServer.args.join(' ') : ''}`;
      output.push(
        `  * ${escapeForDisplay(key)} (${isLocal ? 'local' : 'remote'}): ${escapeForDisplay(source)}`,
      );
      if (mcpServer.cwd) {
        output.push(
          `    Working directory: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.cwd)}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.env && Object.keys(mcpServer.env).length > 0) {
        output.push('    Environment variables:');
        const sortedEnv = Object.entries(mcpServer.env).sort(([a], [b]) =>
          a.localeCompare(b),
        );
        for (const [envKey, envValue] of sortedEnv) {
          const isSensitive = SENSITIVE_ENV_NAME.test(envKey);
          const displayValue =
            isSensitive && envValue
              ? '********'
              : escapeForDisplay(envValue ?? '');
          output.push(`      - ${escapeForDisplay(envKey)}: ${displayValue}`);
        }
      }
      if (mcpServer.headers && Object.keys(mcpServer.headers).length > 0) {
        output.push('    Headers:');
        const sortedHeaders = Object.entries(mcpServer.headers).sort(
          ([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b),
        );
        for (const [headerKey, headerValue] of sortedHeaders) {
          const isSensitive = SENSITIVE_HEADER_NAME.test(headerKey);
          const displayValue =
            isSensitive && headerValue
              ? '********'
              : escapeForDisplay(headerValue ?? '');
          output.push(
            `      - ${escapeForDisplay(headerKey)}: ${displayValue}`,
          );
        }
      }
      if (mcpServer.url) {
        output.push(`    URL: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.url)}`);
      }
      if (mcpServer.tcp) {
        output.push(`    TCP: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.tcp)}`);
      }
      if (mcpServer.type) {
        output.push(`    Type: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.type)}`);
      }
      if (mcpServer.timeout !== undefined) {
        output.push(`    Timeout: ${escapeListForDisplay(mcpServer.timeout)}`);
      }
      if (mcpServer.trust !== undefined) {
        output.push(`    Trust: ${escapeListForDisplay(mcpServer.trust)}`);
      }
      if (mcpServer.description) {
        output.push(
          `    Description: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.description)}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.includeTools && mcpServer.includeTools.length > 0) {
        output.push(
          `    Include tools: ${mcpServer.includeTools.map((tool) => escapeForDisplay(tool)).join(', ')}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.excludeTools && mcpServer.excludeTools.length > 0) {
        output.push(
          `    Exclude tools: ${mcpServer.excludeTools.map((tool) => escapeForDisplay(tool)).join(', ')}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.authProviderType) {
        output.push(
          `    Auth Provider Type: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.authProviderType)}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.targetAudience) {
        output.push(
          `    Target Audience: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.targetAudience)}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.targetServiceAccount) {
        output.push(
          `    Target Service Account: ${escapeForDisplay(mcpServer.targetServiceAccount)}`,
        );
      }
      if (mcpServer.oauth) {
        output.push('    OAuth Configuration:');
        const sortedOauth = Object.entries(mcpServer.oauth).sort(([a], [b]) =>
          a.localeCompare(b),
        );
        for (const [oKey, oValue] of sortedOauth) {
          const isSensitive = SENSITIVE_OAUTH_NAME.test(oKey);
          const valStr = Array.isArray(oValue)
            ? oValue.join(', ')
            : String(oValue ?? '');
          const displayValue =
            isSensitive && valStr ? '********' : escapeForDisplay(valStr);
          output.push(`      - ${escapeForDisplay(oKey)}: ${displayValue}`);
        }
      }
      output.push(`    Config signature: ${getMcpServerConfigHash(mcpServer)}`);
      const serverFiles = mcpServerFiles.get(key);
      if (serverFiles?.filesSignature) {
        output.push(
          `    Files used: ${serverFiles.referencedPaths.map(formatReferencedPath).join(', ')}`,
        );
        output.push(`    Files signature: ${serverFiles.filesSignature}`);
      }
    }
  }
  if (sanitizedConfig.contextFileName) {
    output.push(
      `This extension will append info to your gemini.md context using ${escapeListForDisplay(sanitizedConfig.contextFileName)}`,
    );
  } else if (contentSummary?.contextFiles) {
    output.push(
      'This extension will append info to your gemini.md context using GEMINI.md',
    );
  }
  if (contentSummary?.contextFiles) {
    output.push(...renderContextFilesDetails(contentSummary.contextFiles));
  }
  if (sanitizedConfig.excludeTools) {
    output.push(
      `This extension will exclude the following core tools: ${escapeListForDisplay(sanitizedConfig.excludeTools)}`,
    );
  }
  // With a summary, settings and the plan directory are read as written in
  // the manifest, so they don't depend on where the folder is.
  const settings = contentSummary
    ? contentSummary.settings
    : loadedSettings(sanitizedConfig);
  if (settings && settings.length > 0) {
    output.push(...renderSettings(settings));
  }
  const planDirectory = contentSummary
    ? contentSummary.planDirectory
    : sanitizedConfig.plan?.directory;
  if (planDirectory) {
    output.push(
      `This extension will store plans in ${formatValueForDisplay(planDirectory)}`,
    );
  }
  if (contentSummary) {
    if (contentSummary.hooks) {
      output.push(...renderHooksSection(contentSummary.hooks));
    }
  } else if (hasHooks) {
    output.push(`${HOOKS_HEADING}.`);
  }
  if (contentSummary?.agents) {
    output.push(...renderAgentsSection(contentSummary.agents));
  }
  if (contentSummary?.commands) {
    output.push(
      ...renderFilesSection(
        'This extension will add the following custom commands:',
        'Commands signature',
        contentSummary.commands,
      ),
    );
  }
  if (contentSummary?.policies) {
    output.push(
      ...renderFilesSection(
        'This extension will add the following policy files:',
        'Policies signature',
        contentSummary.policies,
      ),
    );
  }
  const hasSkills = contentSummary
    ? contentSummary.skills !== undefined
    : skills.length > 0;
  if (hasSkills) {
    output.push(`\n${chalk.bold('Agent Skills:')}`);
    output.push('\nThis extension will install the following agent skills:\n');
    output.push(
      ...(contentSummary?.skills
        ? renderSkillSummaries(contentSummary.skills)
        : await renderSkillsList(skills)),
    );
  }
  if (contentSummary?.extensionFiles) {
    output.push(
      `Extension files signature: ${contentSummary.extensionFiles.signature}`,
    );
  }

  if (sanitizedLinkedPath) {
    output.push(
      '\n' +
        chalk.yellow(
          `⚠️  Warning: Linking creates a live symbolic link to "${sanitizedLinkedPath}". Any future changes made to code, MCP servers, hooks, or prompts inside that directory will take effect automatically upon CLI startup without further warnings.`,
        ),
    );
  }
  output.push('\n' + INSTALL_WARNING_MESSAGE);
  if (hasSkills) {
    output.push('\n' + SKILLS_WARNING_MESSAGE);
  }

  return output.join('\n');
}

/**
 * Shared logic for formatting a list of agent skills for a consent prompt.
 */
async function renderSkillsList(skills: SkillDefinition[]): Promise<string[]> {
  const output: string[] = [];
  for (const skill of skills) {
    output.push(`  * ${chalk.bold(skill.name)}: ${skill.description}`);
    const skillDir = path.dirname(skill.location);
    let fileCountStr = '';
    try {
      const skillDirItems = await fs.readdir(skillDir);
      fileCountStr = ` (${skillDirItems.length} items in directory)`;
    } catch {
      fileCountStr = ` ${chalk.red('⚠️ (Could not count items in directory)')}`;
    }
    output.push(chalk.dim(`    (Source: ${skill.location})${fileCountStr}`));
    output.push('');
  }
  return output;
}

/**
 * Requests consent from the user to install an extension (extensionConfig), if
 * there is any difference between the consent string for `extensionConfig` and
 * `previousExtensionConfig`.
 *
 * Always requests consent if previousExtensionConfig is null.
 *
 * Throws if the user does not consent.
 */
export async function maybeRequestConsentOrFail(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  requestConsent: (consent: string) => Promise<boolean>,
  hasHooks: boolean,
  previousExtensionConfig?: ExtensionConfig,
  previousHasHooks?: boolean,
  skills: SkillDefinition[] = [],
  previousSkills: SkillDefinition[] = [],
  isMigrating: boolean = false,
  linkedSourcePath?: string,
  previousLinkedSourcePath?: string,
  contentSummaries?: {
    current: ExtensionContentSummary;
    previous?: ExtensionContentSummary;
  },
) {
  const extensionConsent = await extensionConsentString(
    extensionConfig,
    hasHooks,
    skills,
    previousExtensionConfig?.name,
    isMigrating,
    linkedSourcePath,
    contentSummaries?.current,
  );
  let changes: string[] = [];
  if (previousExtensionConfig) {
    const previousContentSummary = contentSummaries
      ? (contentSummaries.previous ?? {})
      : undefined;
    const previousExtensionConsent = await extensionConsentString(
      previousExtensionConfig,
      previousHasHooks ?? false,
      previousSkills,
      undefined,
      false,
      previousLinkedSourcePath,
      previousContentSummary,
    );
    if (previousExtensionConsent === extensionConsent) {
      return;
    }
    if (contentSummaries && previousContentSummary) {
      changes = describeContentChanges(
        previousContentSummary,
        contentSummaries.current,
      );
    }
  }
  // The change block is shown above the question but isn't compared.
  const consentText =
    changes.length > 0
      ? [extensionConsent, '', CHANGES_HEADING, ...changes].join('\n')
      : extensionConsent;
  if (!(await requestConsent(consentText))) {
    throw new ExtensionConsentDeclinedError(extensionConfig.name);
  }
}

  }

      expect(computeContentSignature([first, second, first])).toBe(

      ['a line separator', 'a\u2028b', 'a\\u2028b'],
      ['a byte order mark', '\ufeffa', '\\ufeffa'],
    ])('escapes %s', (_name, input, expected) => {
      expect(escapeForDisplay(input)).toBe(expected);
    });

    it('keeps printable text unchanged', () => {
      const value = 'node ${extensionPath}/run.js --name="café" 😀 *a* _b_';
      expect(escapeForDisplay(value)).toBe(value);
    });

    it('prints other JSON types the way a template string does, and null or undefined as empty', () => {
      expect(escapeForDisplay(3)).toBe('3');
      expect(escapeForDisplay(false)).toBe('false');
      expect(escapeForDisplay(['a', 'b\nc'])).toBe('a,b\\nc');
      expect(escapeForDisplay(null)).toBe('');
      expect(escapeForDisplay(undefined)).toBe('');
    });
  });

  describe('formatCodeSpan', () => {
    it.each([
      ['plain text', 'echo hi', '`echo hi`'],
      ['a backtick inside', 'a`b', '``a`b``'],
      ['a run of backticks inside', 'a``b', '```a``b```'],
      ['a trailing backtick', 'echo `id`', '`` echo `id` ``'],
      ['a leading backtick', '`start', '`` `start ``'],
      ['spaces on both sides', ' padded ', '`  padded  `'],
      ['only spaces', '   ', '`   `'],
      ['an empty value', '', '``'],
    ])('formats a value with %s', (_name, input, expected) => {
      expect(formatCodeSpan(input)).toBe(expected);
    });
  });

  describe('formatValueForDisplay', () => {
    it('escapes the value before wrapping it in a code span', () => {
      expect(formatValueForDisplay('echo `a`\n\u001b[2J')).toBe(
        '``echo `a`\\n\\u001b[2J``',
      );
    });
  });
});

/**
 * @license
 * Copyright 2026 Google LLC
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { createReadStream, type Stats } from 'node:fs';
import * as fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import * as path from 'node:path';
import { isSubpath } from '@google/gemini-cli-core';

/**
 * Kind of an entry in a content signature:
 * - `file`: a regular file.
 * - `dir`: a folder that was already walked through another path.
 * - `link`: a symbolic link. Links that stay inside the extension folder are
 *   followed; links that leave it or don't resolve get a marker.
 * - `other`: a FIFO, socket, or device. These are never read.
 * - `reference`: a path referenced by a command that can't be read.
 */
export type ContentEntryType = 'file' | 'dir' | 'link' | 'other' | 'reference';

/** Values recorded instead of a SHA-256 hash. */
export enum ContentMarker {
  /** The link points to a folder; its entries follow under the link path. */
  Directory = 'dir',
  /** The path resolves outside the extension folder, so it isn't read. */
  Outside = 'outside',
  /** The link target doesn't exist. */
  Dangling = 'dangling',
  /** The folder was already walked, for example through a link loop. */
  Visited = 'visited',
  /** Not a regular file, folder, or link. */
  Unsupported = 'unsupported',
  /** The path exists but can't be read. */
  Unreadable = 'unreadable',
  /** The referenced path doesn't exist. */
  Missing = 'missing',
  /** The reference points to the extension folder itself. */
  Root = 'root',
}

/** One entry of a content signature. */
export interface ContentEntry {
  /** Path relative to the extension folder, with `/` separators. */
  path: string;
  type: ContentEntryType;
  /** SHA-256 (hex) of the file bytes, or a {@link ContentMarker}. */
  value: string;
}

/** Returns `value` as a {@link ContentMarker}, or `undefined` for a hash. */
export function asContentMarker(value: string): ContentMarker | undefined {
  return Object.values(ContentMarker).find((marker) => marker === value);
}

/**
 * Compares two strings by UTF-16 code units, so the order doesn't depend on
 * the locale.
 */
export function compareCodeUnits(a: string, b: string): number {
  if (a < b) {
    return -1;
  }
  return a > b ? 1 : 0;
}

/** Returns the SHA-256 (hex) of `content`. */
export function sha256(content: string | Uint8Array): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex');
}

/**
 * Returns the SHA-256 (hex) of a file's bytes. The file is read as a stream,
 * so a large file in the extension folder isn't loaded into memory at once.
 */
function hashFile(filePath: string): Promise<string> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const hash = createHash('sha256');
    createReadStream(filePath)
      .on('data', (chunk) => hash.update(chunk))
      .on('end', () => resolve(hash.digest('hex')))
      .on('error', reject);
  });
}

function entryLine(entry: ContentEntry): string {
  return `${entry.path}\0${entry.type}\0${entry.value}`;
}

/**
 * Returns the SHA-256 (hex) of the unique entry lines
 * (`<path>\0<type>\0<value>`), sorted by UTF-16 code units and joined with
 * `\n`.
 */
export function computeContentSignature(
  entries: readonly ContentEntry[],
): string {
  const lines = [...new Set(entries.map(entryLine))].sort(compareCodeUnits);
  return sha256(lines.join('\n'));
}

interface WalkState {
  rootRealPath: string;
  startPath: string;
  startRealPath: string;
  visitedFolders: Set<string>;
  entries: ContentEntry[];
}

function typeOf(stats: Stats): ContentEntryType {
  if (stats.isSymbolicLink()) {
    return 'link';
  }
  if (stats.isDirectory()) {
    return 'dir';
  }
  return stats.isFile() ? 'file' : 'other';
}

async function walk(
  state: WalkState,
  absolutePath: string,
  relativePath: string,
): Promise<void> {
  let stats: Stats;
  try {
    stats = await fs.lstat(absolutePath);
  } catch {
    state.entries.push({
      path: relativePath,
      type: 'reference',
      value: ContentMarker.Missing,
    });
    return;
  }
  const type = typeOf(stats);
  const isLink = type === 'link';

  let realPath: string;
  try {
    realPath = await fs.realpath(absolutePath);
  } catch {
    state.entries.push({
      path: relativePath,
      type,
      value: ContentMarker.Dangling,
    });
    return;
  }
  if (!isSubpath(state.rootRealPath, realPath)) {
    state.entries.push({
      path: relativePath,
      type,
      value: ContentMarker.Outside,
    });
    return;
  }

  try {
    const target = isLink ? await fs.stat(realPath) : stats;
    if (target.isFile()) {
      state.entries.push({
        path: relativePath,
        type,
        value: await hashFile(realPath),
      });
      return;
    }
    if (!target.isDirectory()) {
      state.entries.push({
        path: relativePath,
        type,
        value: ContentMarker.Unsupported,
      });
      return;
    }
    // A link to a folder that holds the starting point (or that was already
    // walked) would walk the same files again, or never end.
    if (
      state.visitedFolders.has(realPath) ||
      (isLink &&
        absolutePath !== state.startPath &&
        isSubpath(realPath, state.startRealPath))
    ) {
      state.entries.push({
        path: relativePath,
        type,
        value: ContentMarker.Visited,
      });
      return;
    }
    state.visitedFolders.add(realPath);
    if (isLink) {
      state.entries.push({
        path: relativePath,
        type,
        value: ContentMarker.Directory,
      });
    }
    const names = (await fs.readdir(realPath)).sort(compareCodeUnits);
    for (const name of names) {
      await walk(state, path.join(realPath, name), `${relativePath}/${name}`);
    }
  } catch {
    state.entries.push({
      path: relativePath,
      type,
      value: ContentMarker.Unreadable,
    });
  }
}

/**
 * Lists the entries of `relativePath`, a file or folder inside `rootDir`
 * given with `/` separators. Regular files are hashed (raw bytes, ignoring
 * permissions and dates) and folders are walked. Links that stay inside
 * `rootDir` are followed; anything else gets a {@link ContentMarker}. Nothing
 * outside `rootDir` is ever read.
 *
 * @returns The entries in walk order, or `undefined` when the path doesn't
 * exist.
 */
export async function collectContentEntries(
  rootDir: string,
  relativePath: string,
): Promise<ContentEntry[] | undefined> {
  const absolutePath = path.join(rootDir, ...relativePath.split('/'));
  let rootRealPath: string;
  try {
    rootRealPath = await fs.realpath(rootDir);
    await fs.lstat(absolutePath);
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
  let startRealPath = absolutePath;
  try {
    startRealPath = await fs.realpath(absolutePath);
  } catch {
    // A dangling link; `walk` records it.
  }
  const state: WalkState = {
    rootRealPath,
    startPath: absolutePath,
    startRealPath,
    visitedFolders: new Set(),
    entries: [],
  };
  await walk(state, absolutePath, relativePath);
  return state.entries;
}

function needsEscape(code: number): boolean {
  return (
    code <= 0x1f ||
    (code >= 0x7f && code <= 0x9f) ||
    (code >= 0x200b && code <= 0x200f) ||
    (code >= 0x2028 && code <= 0x202e) ||
    (code >= 0x2066 && code <= 0x2069) ||
    code === 0xfeff
  );
}

function escapeCodeUnit(code: number): string {
  switch (code) {
    case 0x09:
      return '\\t';
    case 0x0a:
      return '\\n';
    case 0x0d:
      return '\\r';
    default:
      return `\\u${code.toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}`;
  }
}

/**
 * Replaces characters that can hide or reshape text in a terminal with
 * JSON-style escapes (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\u001b`): C0 and C1 controls, DEL,
 * zero-width characters, line and paragraph separators, bidirectional
 * controls, and the byte order mark. The result always fits on one line, and
 * ANSI sequences show as text. Values read from `gemini-extension.json` can
 * have any JSON type, so a value that isn't a string prints the way a template
 * string prints it, and `null` or `undefined` prints as an empty string.
 */
export function escapeForDisplay(value: unknown): string {
  const text = String(value ?? '');
  let result = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) {
    const code = text.charCodeAt(i);
    result += needsEscape(code) ? escapeCodeUnit(code) : text[i];
  }
  return result;
}

/**
 * Wraps `value` in a Markdown code span that renders verbatim. The backtick
 * fence is one longer than the longest run of backticks in the value. Markdown
 * removes one space from each side of a code span when both sides have one, so
 * a space of padding is added when the value starts or ends with a backtick, or
 * starts and ends with a space.
 */
export function formatCodeSpan(value: string): string {
  if (value === '') {
    return '``';
  }
  let longestRun = 0;
  for (const run of value.match(/`+/g) ?? []) {
    longestRun = Math.max(longestRun, run.length);
  }
  const fence = '`'.repeat(longestRun + 1);
  const needsPadding =
    value.startsWith('`') ||
    value.endsWith('`') ||
    (value.startsWith(' ') && value.endsWith(' ') && /[^ ]/.test(value));
  const padding = needsPadding ? ' ' : '';
  return `${fence}${padding}${value}${padding}${fence}`;
}

/**
 * Formats a value read from extension files for the consent text: escaped
 * with {@link escapeForDisplay} and wrapped in a code span with
 * {@link formatCodeSpan}.
 */
export function formatValueForDisplay(value: string): string {
  return formatCodeSpan(escapeForDisplay(value));
}

/**
 * Thrown when the user declines the consent request to install or update an
 * extension. Nothing has been changed on disk when it's thrown.
 */
export class ExtensionConsentDeclinedError extends Error {
  constructor(readonly extensionName: string) {
    super(`Installation cancelled for "${extensionName}".`);
    this.name = 'ExtensionConsentDeclinedError';
  }
}
