import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import * as fs from 'node:fs';
import * as os from 'node:os';
import * as path from 'node:path';
import {
  computeContentSignature,
  ContentMarker,
  sha256,
  type ContentEntry,
} from './contentSignature.js';
import {
  buildExtensionContentSummary,
  findReferencedPaths,
} from './extensionContentSummary.js';

const isWindows = process.platform === 'win32';

const agentLoaderErrors = vi.hoisted(() => {
  const extra: Array<{ filePath: string; message: string }> = [];
  return { extra };
});

// Delegates to the real loader and appends the errors a test sets, to cover
// load errors that the real loader doesn't produce.
vi.mock('@google/gemini-cli-core', async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual =
    await importOriginal<typeof import('@google/gemini-cli-core')>();
  return {
    ...actual,
    loadAgentsFromDirectory: async (dir: string) => {
      const result = await actual.loadAgentsFromDirectory(dir);
      return {
        ...result,
        errors: [
          ...result.errors,
          ...agentLoaderErrors.extra.map(
            ({ filePath, message }) =>
              new actual.AgentLoadError(filePath, message),
          ),
        ],
      };
    },
  };
});

function fileEntry(relativePath: string, content: string): ContentEntry {
  return { path: relativePath, type: 'file', value: sha256(content) };
}

function hooksFile(command: string, env?: Record<string, string>): string {
  return JSON.stringify({
    hooks: {
      SessionStart: [
        { hooks: [{ type: 'command', command, ...(env ? { env } : {}) }] },
      ],
    },
  });
}

describe('extensionContentSummary', () => {
  let tempDir: string;
  let rootDir: string;

  function writeFile(relativePath: string, content: string, root = rootDir) {
    const filePath = path.join(root, relativePath);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(filePath, content);
  }

  beforeEach(() => {
    tempDir = fs.realpathSync(
      fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'extension-content-summary-')),
    );
    rootDir = path.join(tempDir, 'extension');
    fs.mkdirSync(rootDir);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    fs.rmSync(tempDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    agentLoaderErrors.extra = [];
  });

  describe('findReferencedPaths', () => {
    it('finds the paths that follow ${extensionPath}', () => {
      expect(
        findReferencedPaths([
          'node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js --verbose',
          'python3 "${extensionPath}${/}tools${pathSeparator}run.py"',
          '--require=${extensionPath}\\lib\\preload.js',
          'node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js',
        ]),
      ).toEqual([
        { path: 'lib/preload.js' },
        { path: 'scripts/on-start.js' },
        { path: 'tools/run.py' },
      ]);
    });

    it('reads a quoted path up to the matching quote', () => {
      expect(
        findReferencedPaths([
          'node "${extensionPath}/my scripts/on start.js" --verbose',
          "bash '${extensionPath}${/}tools (v2)${/}setup.sh'",
          'cat "${extensionPath}/Bob\'s notes.txt"',
        ]),
      ).toEqual([
        { path: "Bob's notes.txt" },
        { path: 'my scripts/on start.js' },
        { path: 'tools (v2)/setup.sh' },
      ]);
    });

    it('ends a quoted path at a list separator or a variable', () => {
      expect(
        findReferencedPaths([
          'PYTHONPATH="${extensionPath}/lib dir:${extensionPath}/vendor" python3 app.py',
          'node "${extensionPath}/scripts/$NAME.js"',
        ]),
      ).toEqual([{ path: 'lib dir' }, { path: 'scripts' }, { path: 'vendor' }]);
    });

    it('marks references to the folder itself and to paths outside it', () => {
      expect(
        findReferencedPaths([
          'cd ${extensionPath} && ls ${extensionPath}/',
          'cat ${extensionPath}/../other/file',
          'run ${extensionPath}-data/x',
        ]),
      ).toEqual([
        { path: '${extensionPath}-data/x', marker: ContentMarker.Outside },
        { path: '.', marker: ContentMarker.Root },
        { path: '../other/file', marker: ContentMarker.Outside },
      ]);
    });

    it('ignores values without ${extensionPath}', () => {
      expect(findReferencedPaths(['echo hi', '$HOME/run.sh'])).toEqual([]);
    });
  });

  describe('hooks', () => {
    it('is absent without hooks/hooks.json', async () => {
      writeFile('hooks/notes.txt', 'notes');

      expect(
        await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir, { includeAllFiles: false }),
      ).toEqual({});
    });

    it('lists hooks by event name, in file order within an event', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'hooks/hooks.json',
        JSON.stringify({
          hooks: {
            SessionStart: [
              {
                hooks: [
                  { type: 'command', command: 'echo first' },
                  { type: 'command', command: 'echo second', name: 'second' },
                ],
              },
            ],
            BeforeTool: [
              {
                matcher: 'run_shell_command',
                hooks: [
                  {
                    type: 'command',
                    command: 'echo tool',
                    env: { ZED: 'z', ALPHA: 'a' },
                  },
                ],
              },
              'not an object',
              { hooks: 'not a list' },
            ],
            AfterAgent: [{ hooks: [{ type: 'runtime' }, 42] }],
          },
        }),
      );

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(summary.hooks?.hooks).toEqual([
        { eventName: 'AfterAgent', type: 'runtime', env: [] },
        {
          eventName: 'BeforeTool',
          matcher: 'run_shell_command',
          command: 'echo tool',
          env: [
            ['ALPHA', 'a'],
            ['ZED', 'z'],
          ],
        },
        { eventName: 'SessionStart', command: 'echo first', env: [] },
        {
          eventName: 'SessionStart',
          name: 'second',
          command: 'echo second',
          env: [],
        },
      ]);
    });

    it.each([
      ['invalid JSON', '{ "hooks": '],
      ['a hooks value that is not an object', '{ "hooks": [] }'],
    ])(
      'signs a hooks.json file with %s without listing hooks',
      async (_name, content) => {
        writeFile('hooks/hooks.json', content);

        const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

        const files = [fileEntry('hooks/hooks.json', content)];
        expect(summary.hooks).toEqual({
          files,
          referencedPaths: [],
          signature: computeContentSignature(files),
        });
      },
    );

    it('signs the files under hooks/ and the paths that hooks reference', async () => {
      const hooks = hooksFile('node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js', {
        CONFIG_DIR: '${extensionPath}/config',
      });
      writeFile('hooks/hooks.json', hooks);
      writeFile('hooks/helper.sh', 'helper');
      writeFile('scripts/on-start.js', 'start');
      writeFile('config/settings.json', '{}');

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      const configEntries = [fileEntry('config/settings.json', '{}')];
      const scriptEntries = [fileEntry('scripts/on-start.js', 'start')];
      const hookFiles = [
        fileEntry('hooks/helper.sh', 'helper'),
        fileEntry('hooks/hooks.json', hooks),
      ];
      expect(summary.hooks?.files).toEqual(hookFiles);
      expect(summary.hooks?.referencedPaths).toEqual([
        { path: 'config', signature: computeContentSignature(configEntries) },
        {
          path: 'scripts/on-start.js',
          signature: computeContentSignature(scriptEntries),

      ]);
      expect(summary.hooks?.signature).toBe(

          ...hookFiles,
          ...configEntries,
          ...scriptEntries,
        ]),
      );
    });

    it('marks referenced paths that are missing or outside the folder', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'hooks/hooks.json',
        hooksFile(

      );

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(summary.hooks?.referencedPaths).toEqual([

              type: 'reference',
              value: ContentMarker.Outside,
            },
          ]),
        },
        {
          path: 'missing.js',
          marker: ContentMarker.Missing,
          signature: computeContentSignature([
            {
              path: 'missing.js',
              type: 'reference',
              value: ContentMarker.Missing,
            },
          ]),
        },
      ]);
    });

    it.skipIf(isWindows)(

      async () => {
        const outsideDir = path.join(tempDir, 'outside');
        writeFile('data.txt', 'outside data', outsideDir);
        fs.symlinkSync(outsideDir, path.join(rootDir, 'scripts'));
        writeFile(
          'hooks/hooks.json',
          hooksFile('cat ${extensionPath}/scripts/data.txt'),

        const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

        expect(summary.hooks?.referencedPaths).toEqual([

                type: 'file',

              },

          },
        ]);
      },
    );

    it('returns the same summary for identical folders in different places', async () => {
      const otherRoot = path.join(tempDir, 'elsewhere', 'copy');
      for (const root of [rootDir, otherRoot]) {
        writeFile(
          'hooks/hooks.json',
          hooksFile('node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js'),
          root,
        );
        writeFile('scripts/on-start.js', 'start', root);
      }

      expect(await buildExtensionContentSummary(otherRoot)).toEqual(
        await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir),
      );
    });

    it('changes the hooks signature when a referenced script changes', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'hooks/hooks.json',
        hooksFile('node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js'),
      );
      writeFile('scripts/on-start.js', 'v1');
      const before = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      writeFile('scripts/on-start.js', 'v2');
      const after = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(after.hooks?.signature).not.toBe(before.hooks?.signature);
      expect(after.hooks?.files).toEqual(before.hooks?.files);
    });

    it('signs a quoted referenced path that contains spaces', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'hooks/hooks.json',
        hooksFile('node "${extensionPath}/my scripts/on start.js"'),

      writeFile('my scripts/on start.js', 'v1');
      const before = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      writeFile('my scripts/on start.js', 'v2');
      const after = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(before.hooks?.referencedPaths).toEqual([

        },
      ]);
      expect(after.hooks?.signature).not.toBe(before.hooks?.signature);
    });
  });

  describe('context files', () => {

      return {
        contextFilePaths: relativePaths.map((relativePath) =>

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(

        contextSources('GEMINI.md'),

      const files = [

        fileEntry('docs/rules.md', rules),

    it('signs every context file of a list', async () => {

      expect(summary.contextFiles?.paths).toEqual(['a.md', 'b.md']);

        rootDir,
        contextSources('GEMINI.md'),
      );

      expect(summary.contextFiles?.importedPaths).toEqual([]);
      expect(summary.contextFiles?.files).toEqual([
        fileEntry('GEMINI.md', context),
      ]);
    });

    it('finishes and lists each file once when imports form a cycle', async () => {

      writeFile('GEMINI.md', context);

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(
        rootDir,
        contextSources('GEMINI.md'),

      ]);
    });

    it('keeps the imports of a file that a long import chain also reaches', async () => {

      expect(summary.contextFiles?.importedPaths).toEqual([

        'chain2.md',
        'chain3.md',
        'chain4.md',
        'leaf.md',
        'shared.md',
      ]);
    });
  });

        expect(summary.skills?.skills.map((skill) => skill.name)).toEqual([
          'inside',
        ]);
        expect(summary.skills?.files).toContainEqual({
          path: 'skills/linked',
          type: 'link',
          value: ContentMarker.Outside,
        });
      },
    );
  });

  describe('sub-agents', () => {
    const localAgent = [
      '---',
      'name: release-helper',
      'description: Helps with releases',
      'mcp_servers:',
      '  tracker:',
      '    command: node',
      '    args:',
      '      - ${extensionPath}/servers/tracker.js',
      '    trust: true',
      '---',
      'You help with releases.',
    ].join('\n');
    const remoteAgent = [
      '---',
      'kind: remote',
      'name: remote-helper',
      'agent_card_url: https://example.com/card.json',
      '---',
    ].join('\n');

    it('lists the agents that the loader reads, with their MCP servers and the files they use', async () => {
      writeFile('agents/release-helper.md', localAgent);
      writeFile('agents/remote.md', remoteAgent);
      writeFile('agents/broken.md', 'no front matter');
      writeFile('agents/_draft.md', 'skipped');
      writeFile('agents/notes.txt', 'skipped');
      writeFile('agents/nested/deep.md', 'skipped');
      writeFile('servers/tracker.js', 'server');

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      const files = [
        fileEntry('agents/broken.md', 'no front matter'),
        fileEntry('agents/release-helper.md', localAgent),
        fileEntry('agents/remote.md', remoteAgent),
      ];
      const trackerEntries = [fileEntry('servers/tracker.js', 'server')];
      expect(summary.agents?.files).toEqual(files);
      expect(
        summary.agents?.agents.map((agent) => ({
          path: agent.path,
          name: agent.name,
          agentCardUrl: agent.agentCardUrl,
          servers: agent.mcpServers.map(([name, server]) => [
            name,
            server.command,
            server.args,
            server.trust,
          ]),
        })),
      ).toEqual([
        { path: 'agents/broken.md', servers: [] },
        {
          path: 'agents/release-helper.md',
          name: 'release-helper',
          servers: [
            ['tracker', 'node', ['${extensionPath}/servers/tracker.js'], true],
          ],
        },
        {
          path: 'agents/remote.md',
          name: 'remote-helper',
          agentCardUrl: 'https://example.com/card.json',
          servers: [],
        },
      ]);
      expect(summary.agents?.referencedPaths).toEqual([
        {
          path: 'servers/tracker.js',
          signature: computeContentSignature(trackerEntries),
        },
      ]);
      expect(summary.agents?.signature).toBe(
        computeContentSignature([...files, ...trackerEntries]),
      );
    });

    it('lists a load error without a file path under agents', async () => {
      writeFile('agents/release-helper.md', localAgent);
      agentLoaderErrors.extra = [{ filePath: '', message: 'unreadable' }];

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(summary.agents?.agents.map((agent) => agent.path)).toEqual([
        'agents',
        'agents/release-helper.md',
      ]);
    });

    it('is absent when agents/ has no file that the loader reads', async () => {
      writeFile('agents/_draft.md', 'skipped');
      writeFile('agents/README.txt', 'skipped');

      expect(
        await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir, { includeAllFiles: false }),
      ).toEqual({});
    });

    it.skipIf(isWindows)(
      'does not load agents through a folder link that leaves the extension folder',
      async () => {
        const outsideDir = path.join(tempDir, 'outside-agents');
        writeFile('helper.md', localAgent, outsideDir);
        fs.symlinkSync(outsideDir, path.join(rootDir, 'agents'));

        const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

        const files: ContentEntry[] = [
          { path: 'agents', type: 'link', value: ContentMarker.Outside },
        ];
        expect(summary.agents).toEqual({
          agents: [],
          referencedPaths: [],
          files,
          signature: computeContentSignature(files),
        });
      },
    );
  });

  describe('custom commands and policies', () => {
    it('lists the commands that the loader finds, including nested and hidden folders', async () => {
      writeFile('commands/deploy.toml', 'a');
      writeFile('commands/release/notes.toml', 'b');
      writeFile('commands/.internal/sync.toml', 'c');
      writeFile('commands/README.md', 'skipped');

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      const files = [
        fileEntry('commands/.internal/sync.toml', 'c'),
        fileEntry('commands/deploy.toml', 'a'),
        fileEntry('commands/release/notes.toml', 'b'),
      ];
      expect(summary.commands).toEqual({
        files,
        signature: computeContentSignature(files),
      });
    });

    it('lists the policy files directly in policies/', async () => {
      writeFile('policies/release.toml', 'a');
      writeFile('policies/nested/skipped.toml', 'b');
      writeFile('policies/notes.md', 'c');

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      const files = [fileEntry('policies/release.toml', 'a')];
      expect(summary.policies).toEqual({
        files,
        signature: computeContentSignature(files),
      });
    });
  });

  describe('MCP servers', () => {
    it('keeps ${extensionPath} and ${workspacePath} as written and resolves path separators', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify({
          name: 'demo',
          version: '1.0.0',
          mcpServers: {
            nodeServer: {
              command: 'node',
              args: [
                '${extensionPath}${/}example.js',
                '--root=${workspacePath}${pathSeparator}src',
              ],
              cwd: '${extensionPath}',
            },
          },
        }),
      );
      writeFile('example.js', 'server');

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      const rootEntries: ContentEntry[] = [
        { path: '.', type: 'reference', value: ContentMarker.Root },
      ];
      const entries = [fileEntry('example.js', 'server')];
      expect(summary.mcpServers).toEqual([
        [
          'nodeServer',
          {
            config: {
              command: 'node',
              args: [
                '${extensionPath}/example.js',
                '--root=${workspacePath}/src',
              ],
              cwd: '${extensionPath}',
            },
            referencedPaths: [
              {
                path: '.',
                marker: ContentMarker.Root,
                signature: computeContentSignature(rootEntries),
              },
              {
                path: 'example.js',
                signature: computeContentSignature(entries),
              },
            ],
            filesSignature: computeContentSignature([
              ...rootEntries,
              ...entries,
            ]),
          },
        ],
      ]);
    });

    it('counts the working directory among the files that a server uses', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify({
          name: 'demo',
          version: '1.0.0',
          mcpServers: {
            srv: {
              command: 'node',
              args: ['server.js'],
              cwd: '${extensionPath}/server',
            },
          },
        }),
      );
      writeFile('server/server.js', 'v1');
      const before = (await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir))
        .mcpServers?.[0]?.[1];
      writeFile('server/server.js', 'v2');
      const after = (await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir))
        .mcpServers?.[0]?.[1];

      expect(
        before?.referencedPaths.map((reference) => reference.path),
      ).toEqual(['server']);
      expect(before?.filesSignature).toBe(
        computeContentSignature([fileEntry('server/server.js', 'v1')]),
      );
      expect(after?.filesSignature).not.toBe(before?.filesSignature);
    });

    it('lists no MCP servers when the manifest declares none', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify({ name: 'demo', version: '1.0.0' }),
      );

      expect((await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir)).mcpServers).toEqual(
        [],
      );
    });
  });

  describe('settings and plan directory', () => {
    it('reads the settings and the plan directory as written in the manifest', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify({
          name: 'demo',
          version: '1.0.0',
          settings: [
            {
              name: 'API key',
              description: 'The key',
              envVar: 'API_KEY',
              sensitive: true,
            },
            { name: 'Region', description: 'The region', envVar: 'REGION' },
          ],
          plan: { directory: '${extensionPath}/plans' },
        }),
      );

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(summary.settings).toEqual([
        { name: 'API key', envVar: 'API_KEY', sensitive: true },
        { name: 'Region', envVar: 'REGION', sensitive: false },
      ]);
      expect(summary.planDirectory).toBe('${extensionPath}/plans');
    });
  });

  describe('extension files', () => {
    it('lists every file except .git folders and the files that Gemini CLI writes there', async () => {
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        '{"name": "demo", "version": "1.0.0"}',
      );
      writeFile('lib/helper.js', 'helper');
      writeFile('vendor/tool/index.js', 'tool');
      writeFile('vendor/tool/.git/HEAD', 'ref');
      writeFile('.git/HEAD', 'ref');
      writeFile('.gemini-extension-install.json', '{}');
      writeFile('.env', 'API_KEY=value');

      const summary = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(summary.extensionFiles?.files.map((entry) => entry.path)).toEqual([
        'gemini-extension.json',
        'lib/helper.js',
        'vendor/tool/index.js',
      ]);
    });

    it('hashes gemini-extension.json without its version and with sorted keys', async () => {
      const otherRoot = path.join(tempDir, 'other');
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify({ name: 'demo', version: '1.0.0', description: 'Demo' }),
      );
      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify(
          { description: 'Demo', version: '2.0.0', name: 'demo' },
          null,
          2,
        ),
        otherRoot,
      );
      const signature = (await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir))
        .extensionFiles?.signature;

      expect(
        (await buildExtensionContentSummary(otherRoot)).extensionFiles
          ?.signature,
      ).toBe(signature);

      writeFile(
        'gemini-extension.json',
        JSON.stringify({ name: 'demo', version: '2.0.0', description: 'New' }),
        otherRoot,
      );
      expect(
        (await buildExtensionContentSummary(otherRoot)).extensionFiles
          ?.signature,
      ).not.toBe(signature);
    });

    it('changes when a file that only a script loads changes', async () => {
      writeFile('lib/helper.js', 'v1');
      const before = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);
      writeFile('lib/helper.js', 'v2');

      const after = await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir);

      expect(after.extensionFiles?.signature).not.toBe(
        before.extensionFiles?.signature,
      );
    });

    it('is left out when includeAllFiles is false', async () => {
      writeFile('lib/helper.js', 'helper');

      expect(
        (
          await buildExtensionContentSummary(rootDir, {
            includeAllFiles: false,
          })
        ).extensionFiles,
      ).toBeUndefined();
    });
  });
});

import * as fs from 'node:fs/promises';

  loadAgentsFromDirectory,
  loadSkillFromFile,
  processImports,
  type MCPServerConfig,

  asContentMarker,
  collectContentEntries,
  compareCodeUnits,
  computeContentSignature,
  ContentMarker,

import {
  EXTENSION_SETTINGS_FILENAME,
  INSTALL_METADATA_FILENAME,

/** A path that a command or variable references through `${extensionPath}`. */
export interface ReferencedPath {
  /**
   * Path relative to the extension folder, with `/` separators. `.` is the
   * folder itself, and a path outside it keeps its relative form (`../x`).
   */
  path: string;
  /** Set when the path isn't read, for example because it's missing. */
  marker?: ContentMarker;
  /** Signature of the referenced file or folder. */
  signature: string;
}

/** One hook from `hooks/hooks.json`, with its values as written. */
export interface HookSummary {
  eventName: string;
  matcher?: string;
  name?: string;
  /** The command of a `command` hook. */
  command?: string;
  /** The hook type, for a hook without a command. */
  type?: string;
  /** Environment variables, sorted by name. */
  env: Array<[string, string]>;
}

/** The hooks that `hooks/hooks.json` declares and the files they use. */
export interface HooksSummary {
  /** Hooks in display order, or `undefined` if `hooks/hooks.json` isn't valid. */
  hooks?: HookSummary[];
  /** Every file under `hooks/`. */
  files: ContentEntry[];
  /** Paths that hook commands and environment variables reference. */
  referencedPaths: ReferencedPath[];
  /** Signature of the files under `hooks/` and the referenced paths. */
  signature: string;
}

/**
 * The context files that an extension adds to the model context, and the
 * files that they import.
 */
export interface ContextFilesSummary {
  /** Context files that exist, relative to the extension folder. */
  paths: string[];
  /** Files that the context files import with `@`, relative to the folder. */
  importedPaths: string[];
  /** Entries of the context files and the imported files. */
  files: ContentEntry[];
  signature: string;
}

/**
 * What an extension folder adds to the CLI, read from the raw files on disk
 * without resolving variables, so two folders with the same files have the same
 * summary.
 */
export interface ExtensionContentSummary {
  hooks?: HooksSummary;
  contextFiles?: ContextFilesSummary;
  skills?: SkillsSummary;
  agents?: AgentsSummary;
  commands?: FilesSummary;
  policies?: FilesSummary;
  /** MCP servers of `gemini-extension.json`, in file order. */
  mcpServers?: Array<[string, McpServerSummary]>;
  /** Settings of `gemini-extension.json`, in file order. */
  settings?: SettingSummary[];
  /** `plan.directory` of `gemini-extension.json`, as written. */
  planDirectory?: string;
  /**
   * Every file in the folder, so a change to any of them shows. `.git` folders
   * and the files that Gemini CLI writes there are left out, and
   * `gemini-extension.json` is hashed without its `version`.
   */
  extensionFiles?: FilesSummary;
}

/** One setting from `gemini-extension.json`, with its values as written. */
export interface SettingSummary {
  name: string;
  /** The environment variable that the setting's value is passed in. */
  envVar: string;
  sensitive: boolean;
}

/** One MCP server from `gemini-extension.json`. */
export interface McpServerSummary {
  /**
   * The values as written. Only `${/}` and `${pathSeparator}` are resolved, to
   * `/`, so the values don't depend on where the folder is.
   */
  config: MCPServerConfig;
  /** Paths that the command, args, cwd, and env values reference. */
  referencedPaths: ReferencedPath[];
  /** Signature of the referenced paths, when there are any. */
  filesSignature?: string;
}

/** One sub-agent from `agents/`, with its values as written. */
export interface AgentSummary {
  /** The agent file, relative to the extension folder. */
  path: string;
  /** The agent name, or `undefined` if the file can't be loaded. */
  name?: string;
  /** The agent card URL of a remote agent. */
  agentCardUrl?: string;
  /** MCP servers of a local agent, sorted by name. */
  mcpServers: Array<[string, MCPServerConfig]>;
}

/** The sub-agents under `agents/` and the files that they use. */
export interface AgentsSummary {
  /** Agents sorted by file and name. */
  agents: AgentSummary[];
  /** Paths that the MCP servers of the agents reference. */
  referencedPaths: ReferencedPath[];
  /** The files that the agent loader reads. */
  files: ContentEntry[];
  signature: string;
}

/** Files of one kind, such as custom commands or policy files. */
export interface FilesSummary {
  files: ContentEntry[];
  signature: string;
}

/** One agent skill from the `skills/` folder. */
export interface SkillSummary {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  /** The `SKILL.md` file of the skill, relative to the extension folder. */
  location: string;
  /** Number of items in the skill folder, or `undefined` if it can't be read. */
  itemCount?: number;
  /** Signature of the files in the skill folder. */
  signature: string;
}

/** The agent skills under `skills/`. */
export interface SkillsSummary {
  /** Skills sorted by location. */
  skills: SkillSummary[];
  /** Every file under `skills/`. */
  files: ContentEntry[];
  signature: string;
}

/** Inputs that the extension manager resolves for a folder. */
export interface ExtensionContentSources {
  /** Context files that exist, as returned by `resolveContextFilePaths`. */
  contextFilePaths?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Whether to summarize every file of the folder (default `true`). Linked
   * extensions skip it: they run their source folder as it is and never
   * update, and that folder can be large.
   */
  includeAllFiles?: boolean;
}

const EXTENSION_PATH_VARIABLE = '${extensionPath}';
const PATH_SEPARATOR_VARIABLES = /\$\{(?:\/|pathSeparator)\}/g;
const PATH_END = /[\s"'`;|&<>(),:$]/;
/** Ends a path that follows a quote, along with the matching quote. */
const QUOTED_PATH_END = /[\r\n`;,:$]/;
const SHA256_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;
const HOOKS_FILE = 'hooks/hooks.json';
const MANIFEST_FILE = 'gemini-extension.json';
const SKILL_FILE = 'SKILL.md';
/** Files that Gemini CLI writes in an installed extension folder. */
const CLI_FILES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  INSTALL_METADATA_FILENAME,
  EXTENSION_SETTINGS_FILENAME,
]);
/** Platforms where the skill loader's glob matches names in any case. */
const CASE_INSENSITIVE_GLOB =
  process.platform === 'darwin' || process.platform === 'win32';

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function toRelativePath(rootDir: string, filePath: string): string {
  return path.relative(rootDir, filePath).split(path.sep).join('/');
}

function isInFolder(entry: ContentEntry, folder: string): boolean {
  return entry.path === folder || entry.path.startsWith(`${folder}/`);
}

function toArray(value: unknown): unknown[] {
  return Array.isArray(value) ? value : [];
}

/** Returns a value read from JSON as text, or `undefined` if it's missing. */
function asText(value: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (value === undefined) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : JSON.stringify(value);
}

/** Returns true for a link that leaves the extension folder or is broken. */
export function isUnresolvedLink(entry: ContentEntry): boolean {
  return (
    entry.type === 'link' &&
    (entry.value === ContentMarker.Outside ||
      entry.value === ContentMarker.Dangling)
  );
}

/**
 * Keeps the regular files directly in `folder` whose names pass `accept`, like
 * loaders that list a folder and skip links, plus the entry of the folder
 * itself when it's a link.
 */
function topLevelFiles(
  entries: readonly ContentEntry[],
  folder: string,
  accept: (name: string) => boolean,
): ContentEntry[] {
  return entries.filter((entry) => {
    if (entry.path === folder) {
      return entry.type === 'link';
    }
    const name = entry.path.slice(folder.length + 1);
    return !name.includes('/') && entry.type === 'file' && accept(name);
  });
}

/** Returns true if `files` has more than the link entry of a folder. */
function hasListedFiles(files: readonly ContentEntry[]): boolean {
  return files.some((entry) => entry.value !== ContentMarker.Directory);
}

/**
 * Values of an MCP server that can reference files: command, args, the working
 * directory, and env.
 */
export function mcpServerValues(server: {
  command?: unknown;
  args?: unknown;
  cwd?: unknown;
  env?: unknown;
}): string[] {
  const values: unknown[] = [
    server.command,
    ...toArray(server.args),
    server.cwd,
    ...(isRecord(server.env) ? Object.values(server.env) : []),
  ];
  return values.filter((value): value is string => typeof value === 'string');
}

/** Resolves `${/}` and `${pathSeparator}` to `/` in every string of `value`. */
function resolvePathSeparators(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    return value.replace(PATH_SEPARATOR_VARIABLES, '/');
  }
  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    return value.map(resolvePathSeparators);
  }
  if (isRecord(value)) {
    return Object.fromEntries(
      Object.entries(value).map(([key, item]) => [
        key,
        resolvePathSeparators(item),
      ]),
    );
  }
  return value;
}

function isMcpServerRecord(
  value: unknown,
): value is Record<string, MCPServerConfig> {
  return isRecord(value) && Object.values(value).every(isRecord);
}

function toReferencedPath(suffix: string): Omit<ReferencedPath, 'signature'> {
  const posixSuffix = suffix.replaceAll('\\', '/');
  if (posixSuffix !== '' && !posixSuffix.startsWith('/')) {
    // For example `${extensionPath}-data/x`, a sibling of the extension folder.
    return {
      path: `${EXTENSION_PATH_VARIABLE}${posixSuffix}`,
      marker: ContentMarker.Outside,
    };
  }
  const relativePath = path.posix
    .normalize(`.${posixSuffix}`)
    .replace(/\/+$/, '');
  if (relativePath === '' || relativePath === '.') {
    return { path: '.', marker: ContentMarker.Root };
  }
  if (relativePath === '..' || relativePath.startsWith('../')) {
    return { path: relativePath, marker: ContentMarker.Outside };
  }
  return { path: relativePath };
}

/**
 * Finds the paths that `values` reference through `${extensionPath}`, sorted
 * by UTF-16 code units. `${/}` and `${pathSeparator}` count as `/`, and each
 * path ends at whitespace, a quote, or a shell operator. A path that follows a
 * quote ends at the matching quote instead, so it can contain spaces and shell
 * operators. Every path ends at a line break, `$`, a backtick, or a list
 * separator (`:`, `;`, `,`).
 */
export function findReferencedPaths(
  values: readonly string[],
): Array<Omit<ReferencedPath, 'signature'>> {
  const found = new Map<string, Omit<ReferencedPath, 'signature'>>();
  for (const value of values) {
    const text = value.replace(PATH_SEPARATOR_VARIABLES, '/');
    let start = text.indexOf(EXTENSION_PATH_VARIABLE);
    while (start !== -1) {
      const before = text.charAt(start - 1);
      const quote = before === '"' || before === "'" ? before : undefined;
      const pathEnd = quote ? QUOTED_PATH_END : PATH_END;
      let end = start + EXTENSION_PATH_VARIABLE.length;
      while (
        end < text.length &&
        text[end] !== quote &&
        !pathEnd.test(text[end])
      ) {
        end++;
      }
      const reference = toReferencedPath(
        text.slice(start + EXTENSION_PATH_VARIABLE.length, end),
      );
      found.set(reference.path, reference);
      start = text.indexOf(EXTENSION_PATH_VARIABLE, end);
    }
  }
  return [...found.values()].sort((a, b) => compareCodeUnits(a.path, b.path));
}

/**
 * Hashes the referenced paths inside `rootDir`. A path that is the folder
 * itself, leaves it, or doesn't exist is recorded with a marker and isn't read.
 */
export async function collectReferencedPaths(
  rootDir: string,
  references: ReadonlyArray<Omit<ReferencedPath, 'signature'>>,
): Promise<{ referencedPaths: ReferencedPath[]; entries: ContentEntry[] }> {
  const referencedPaths: ReferencedPath[] = [];
  const entries: ContentEntry[] = [];
  for (const reference of references) {
    let found = reference.marker
      ? undefined
      : await collectContentEntries(rootDir, reference.path);
    let marker = reference.marker;
    if (!found) {
      marker ??= ContentMarker.Missing;
      found = [{ path: reference.path, type: 'reference', value: marker }];
    } else if (found.length === 1 && found[0].path === reference.path) {
      // For example a link that leaves the folder.
      const entryMarker = asContentMarker(found[0].value);
      if (entryMarker && entryMarker !== ContentMarker.Directory) {
        marker = entryMarker;
      }
    }
    referencedPaths.push({
      path: reference.path,
      ...(marker ? { marker } : {}),
      signature: computeContentSignature(found),
    });
    entries.push(...found);
  }
  return { referencedPaths, entries };
}

/** Returns true if `entries` has a hash (not a marker) for `relativePath`. */
export function hasReadableFile(
  entries: readonly ContentEntry[],
  relativePath: string,
): boolean {
  return entries.some(
    (entry) => entry.path === relativePath && SHA256_PATTERN.test(entry.value),
  );
}

/** Reads a text file inside `rootDir`, or returns `undefined` on failure. */
export async function readTextFile(
  rootDir: string,
  relativePath: string,
): Promise<string | undefined> {
  try {
    return await fs.readFile(
      path.join(rootDir, ...relativePath.split('/')),
      'utf-8',
    );
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

function parseEnv(value: unknown): Array<[string, string]> {
  if (!isRecord(value)) {
    return [];
  }
  return Object.keys(value)
    .sort(compareCodeUnits)
    .map((name) => [name, asText(value[name]) ?? '']);
}

/**
 * Lists the hooks of a `hooks/hooks.json` file: events sorted by name, and the
 * hooks of each event in file order. Returns `undefined` if the file isn't
 * valid JSON or `hooks` isn't an object.
 */
export function parseHooksFile(content: string): HookSummary[] | undefined {
  let parsed: unknown;
  try {
    parsed = JSON.parse(content);
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
  if (!isRecord(parsed) || !isRecord(parsed['hooks'])) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const hooksByEvent = parsed['hooks'];
  const hooks: HookSummary[] = [];
  for (const eventName of Object.keys(hooksByEvent).sort(compareCodeUnits)) {
    for (const definition of toArray(hooksByEvent[eventName])) {
      if (!isRecord(definition)) {
        continue;
      }
      const matcher = asText(definition['matcher']);
      for (const hook of toArray(definition['hooks'])) {
        if (!isRecord(hook)) {
          continue;
        }
        const name = asText(hook['name']);
        const command = asText(hook['command']);
        hooks.push({
          eventName,
          ...(matcher !== undefined ? { matcher } : {}),
          ...(name !== undefined ? { name } : {}),
          ...(command !== undefined
            ? { command }
            : { type: asText(hook['type']) ?? '' }),
          env: parseEnv(hook['env']),
        });
      }
    }
  }
  return hooks;
}

async function summarizeHooks(
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<HooksSummary | undefined> {
  try {
    await fs.stat(path.join(rootDir, 'hooks', 'hooks.json'));
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
  const files = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, 'hooks')) ?? [];
  let hooks: HookSummary[] | undefined;
  if (hasReadableFile(files, HOOKS_FILE)) {
    const content = await readTextFile(rootDir, HOOKS_FILE);
    hooks = content === undefined ? undefined : parseHooksFile(content);
  }
  const { referencedPaths, entries } = await collectReferencedPaths(
    rootDir,
    findReferencedPaths(
      (hooks ?? []).flatMap((hook) => [
        hook.command ?? '',
        ...hook.env.map(([, value]) => value),
      ]),
    ),
  );
  return {
    ...(hooks ? { hooks } : {}),
    files,
    referencedPaths,
    signature: computeContentSignature([...files, ...entries]),
  };
}

/**
 * Summarizes the context files and the files they import with `@`. Imports
 * that resolve outside the extension folder aren't read.
 */
async function summarizeContextFiles(
  rootDir: string,
  contextFilePaths: readonly string[],
): Promise<ContextFilesSummary | undefined> {
  if (contextFilePaths.length === 0) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const toRelative = (filePath: string) => toRelativePath(rootDir, filePath);
  const paths = [...new Set(contextFilePaths.map(toRelative))];
  const files: ContentEntry[] = [];
  const imported = new Set<string>();
  for (const relativePath of paths) {
    const entries = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, relativePath)) ?? [
      { path: relativePath, type: 'reference', value: ContentMarker.Missing },
    ];
    files.push(...entries);
    const content = hasReadableFile(entries, relativePath)
      ? await readTextFile(rootDir, relativePath)
      : undefined;
    if (content === undefined) {
      continue;
    }
    const filePath = path.join(rootDir, ...relativePath.split('/'));
    const { importTree } = await processImports(
      content,
      path.dirname(filePath),
      false,
      undefined,
      rootDir,
      'tree',
    );
    // processImports returns a finite tree: it stops at depth 5, skips files
    // that are already in the current import chain, and creates a new node
    // for each import, so this loop ends after visiting each node once. A
    // file can appear more than once, for example as a leaf where the depth
    // limit cuts a chain and again with its own imports, so skipping paths
    // that were already seen would drop those imports.
    const pending = [...(importTree.imports ?? [])];
    for (let node = pending.pop(); node; node = pending.pop()) {
      imported.add(toRelative(node.path));
      pending.push(...(node.imports ?? []));
    }
  }
  const importedPaths = [...imported]
    .filter((importedPath) => !paths.includes(importedPath))
    .sort(compareCodeUnits);
  for (const importedPath of importedPaths) {
    files.push(...((await collectContentEntries(rootDir, importedPath)) ?? []));
  }
  return {
    paths,
    importedPaths,
    files,
    signature: computeContentSignature(files),
  };
}

/**
 * Returns true for the files that `loadSkillsFromDir` loads from `skills/`:
 * `SKILL.md` and `<folder>/SKILL.md`, where its glob skips hidden folders and
 * `node_modules`.
 */
function isSkillFile(relativePath: string): boolean {
  const parts = relativePath.split('/');
  if (parts[0] !== 'skills' || parts.length < 2 || parts.length > 3) {
    return false;
  }
  const fileName = parts[parts.length - 1];
  const isSkillName = CASE_INSENSITIVE_GLOB
    ? fileName.toLowerCase() === SKILL_FILE.toLowerCase()
    : fileName === SKILL_FILE;
  const folder = parts.length === 3 ? parts[1] : '';
  return isSkillName && !folder.startsWith('.') && folder !== 'node_modules';
}

/**
 * Summarizes the skills that `loadSkillsFromDir` finds under `skills/`, with
 * paths relative to the extension folder and a signature over every file of
 * that folder. The loader follows links, so the skills are read here only from
 * the `SKILL.md` files that were hashed inside the extension folder; links that
 * leave it or are broken stay in `files` with a marker and aren't read.
 */
async function summarizeSkills(
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<SkillsSummary | undefined> {
  const files = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, 'skills')) ?? [];
  const skills: SkillSummary[] = [];
  for (const entry of files) {
    if (!isSkillFile(entry.path) || !SHA256_PATTERN.test(entry.value)) {
      continue;
    }
    const definition = await loadSkillFromFile(
      path.join(rootDir, ...entry.path.split('/')),
    );
    if (!definition) {
      continue;
    }
    const folder = path.posix.dirname(entry.path);
    let itemCount: number | undefined;
    try {
      itemCount = (await fs.readdir(path.join(rootDir, ...folder.split('/'))))
        .length;
    } catch {
      // The consent text says that the items can't be counted.
    }
    skills.push({
      name: definition.name,
      description: definition.description,
      location: entry.path,
      ...(itemCount !== undefined ? { itemCount } : {}),
      signature: computeContentSignature(
        files.filter((item) => isInFolder(item, folder)),
      ),
    });
  }
  if (skills.length === 0 && !files.some(isUnresolvedLink)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  skills.sort((a, b) => compareCodeUnits(a.location, b.location));
  return { skills, files, signature: computeContentSignature(files) };
}

/**
 * Summarizes the sub-agents that `loadAgentsFromDirectory` reads: the `.md`
 * files directly in `agents/` whose names don't start with `_`. The agents
 * aren't loaded when `agents/` is a link that leaves the extension folder.
 */
async function summarizeAgents(
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<AgentsSummary | undefined> {
  const entries = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, 'agents')) ?? [];
  const files = topLevelFiles(
    entries,
    'agents',
    (name) => name.endsWith('.md') && !name.startsWith('_'),
  );
  if (!hasListedFiles(files)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const agents: AgentSummary[] = [];
  if (!files.some(isUnresolvedLink)) {
    const loaded = await loadAgentsFromDirectory(path.join(rootDir, 'agents'));
    for (const agent of loaded?.agents ?? []) {
      const filePath = agent.metadata?.filePath;
      agents.push({
        path: filePath ? toRelativePath(rootDir, filePath) : 'agents',
        name: agent.name,
        ...(agent.kind === 'remote' && agent.agentCardUrl
          ? { agentCardUrl: agent.agentCardUrl }
          : {}),
        mcpServers:
          agent.kind === 'local'
            ? Object.entries(agent.mcpServers ?? {}).sort(([a], [b]) =>
                compareCodeUnits(a, b),
              )
            : [],
      });
    }
    for (const error of loaded?.errors ?? []) {
      agents.push({
        path: error.filePath
          ? toRelativePath(rootDir, error.filePath)
          : 'agents',
        mcpServers: [],
      });
    }
  }
  agents.sort(
    (a, b) =>
      compareCodeUnits(a.path, b.path) ||
      compareCodeUnits(a.name ?? '', b.name ?? ''),
  );
  const { referencedPaths, entries: referencedEntries } =
    await collectReferencedPaths(
      rootDir,
      findReferencedPaths(
        agents.flatMap((agent) =>
          agent.mcpServers.flatMap(([, server]) => mcpServerValues(server)),
        ),
      ),
    );
  return {
    agents,
    referencedPaths,
    files,
    signature: computeContentSignature([...files, ...referencedEntries]),
  };
}

/**
 * Summarizes the `.toml` files under `commands/`, like the `**\/*.toml` glob
 * of the command loader, which includes hidden folders and follows links.
 */
async function summarizeCommands(
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<FilesSummary | undefined> {
  const entries = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, 'commands')) ?? [];
  const files = entries.filter(
    (entry) =>
      entry.type !== 'dir' &&
      entry.value !== ContentMarker.Directory &&
      (entry.path.endsWith('.toml') || isUnresolvedLink(entry)),
  );
  return files.length > 0
    ? { files, signature: computeContentSignature(files) }
    : undefined;
}

/**
 * Summarizes the policy files that the policy loader reads: the `.toml` files
 * directly in `policies/`.
 */
async function summarizePolicies(
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<FilesSummary | undefined> {
  const entries = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, 'policies')) ?? [];
  const files = topLevelFiles(entries, 'policies', (name) =>
    name.endsWith('.toml'),
  );
  return hasListedFiles(files)
    ? { files, signature: computeContentSignature(files) }
    : undefined;
}

/**
 * Reads the raw `gemini-extension.json`, or returns `undefined` when it can't
 * be read or isn't a JSON object, so callers can use the loaded values.
 */
async function readManifest(
  rootDir: string,
): Promise<Record<string, unknown> | undefined> {
  const entries = (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, MANIFEST_FILE)) ?? [];
  const content = hasReadableFile(entries, MANIFEST_FILE)
    ? await readTextFile(rootDir, MANIFEST_FILE)
    : undefined;
  if (content === undefined) {
    return undefined;
  }
  try {
    const manifest: unknown = JSON.parse(content);
    return isRecord(manifest) ? manifest : undefined;
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

/**
 * Summarizes the MCP servers of the raw manifest, keeping `${extensionPath}`
 * and `${workspacePath}` as written.
 */
async function summarizeMcpServers(
  rootDir: string,
  manifest: Record<string, unknown>,
): Promise<Array<[string, McpServerSummary]> | undefined> {
  const rawServers = resolvePathSeparators(manifest['mcpServers'] ?? {});
  if (!isMcpServerRecord(rawServers)) {
    return undefined;
  }
  const servers: Array<[string, McpServerSummary]> = [];
  for (const [name, config] of Object.entries(rawServers)) {
    const { referencedPaths, entries: referencedEntries } =
      await collectReferencedPaths(
        rootDir,
        findReferencedPaths(mcpServerValues(config)),
      );
    servers.push([
      name,
      {
        config,
        referencedPaths,
        ...(referencedPaths.length > 0
          ? { filesSignature: computeContentSignature(referencedEntries) }
          : {}),
      },
    ]);
  }
  return servers;
}

/**
 * Lists the settings of the raw manifest. The extension receives each value in
 * the setting's environment variable, in its hooks and MCP servers.
 */
function summarizeSettings(
  manifest: Record<string, unknown>,
): SettingSummary[] | undefined {
  const settings = toArray(manifest['settings'])
    .filter(isRecord)
    .map((setting) => ({
      name: asText(setting['name']) ?? '',
      envVar: asText(setting['envVar']) ?? '',
      sensitive: setting['sensitive'] === true,
    }));
  return settings.length > 0 ? settings : undefined;
}

/** Returns `plan.directory` of the raw manifest, as written. */
function readPlanDirectory(
  manifest: Record<string, unknown>,
): string | undefined {
  const plan = manifest['plan'];
  return isRecord(plan) ? asText(plan['directory']) : undefined;
}

/** Returns the JSON of `value` with object keys sorted by code units. */
function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string {
  return JSON.stringify(value, (_key, item: unknown) =>
    isRecord(item)
      ? Object.fromEntries(
          Object.keys(item)
            .sort(compareCodeUnits)
            .map((key) => [key, item[key]]),
        )
      : item,
  );
}

/**
 * Summarizes every file in the extension folder, so an update that changes a
 * file asks again even when nothing declares it, for example a module that a
 * hook script imports. `.git` folders, `.gemini-extension-install.json`, and
 * `.env` (the settings that Gemini CLI stores there) are left out. When
 * `gemini-extension.json` is valid JSON, its entry is the hash of its content
 * without `version`, with sorted keys, so an update that only changes the
 * version doesn't ask again.
 */
async function summarizeExtensionFiles(
  rootDir: string,
  manifest: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
): Promise<FilesSummary | undefined> {
  let names: string[];
  try {
    names = (await fs.readdir(rootDir)).sort(compareCodeUnits);
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
  const files: ContentEntry[] = [];
  for (const name of names) {
    if (name === '.git' || CLI_FILES.has(name)) {
      continue;
    }
    for (const entry of (await collectContentEntries(rootDir, name)) ?? []) {
      if (entry.path.split('/').includes('.git')) {
        continue;
      }
      if (
        entry.path === MANIFEST_FILE &&
        manifest &&
        SHA256_PATTERN.test(entry.value)
      ) {
        const withoutVersion = { ...manifest };
        delete withoutVersion['version'];
        files.push({ ...entry, value: sha256(canonicalJson(withoutVersion)) });
      } else {
        files.push(entry);
      }
    }
  }
  return files.length > 0
    ? { files, signature: computeContentSignature(files) }
    : undefined;
}

/**
 * Builds the summary of an extension folder from its raw files. Variables such
 * as `${extensionPath}` stay as written, and nothing outside the folder is
 * read.
 */
export async function buildExtensionContentSummary(
  extensionDir: string,
  sources: ExtensionContentSources = {},
): Promise<ExtensionContentSummary> {
  const manifest = await readManifest(extensionDir);
  const hooks = await summarizeHooks(extensionDir);
  const contextFiles = await summarizeContextFiles(
    extensionDir,
    sources.contextFilePaths ?? [],
  );
  const skills = await summarizeSkills(extensionDir);
  const agents = await summarizeAgents(extensionDir);
  const commands = await summarizeCommands(extensionDir);
  const policies = await summarizePolicies(extensionDir);
  const mcpServers = manifest
    ? await summarizeMcpServers(extensionDir, manifest)
    : undefined;
  const settings = manifest ? summarizeSettings(manifest) : undefined;
  const planDirectory = manifest ? readPlanDirectory(manifest) : undefined;
  const extensionFiles =
    sources.includeAllFiles === false
      ? undefined
      : await summarizeExtensionFiles(extensionDir, manifest);
  return {
    ...(hooks ? { hooks } : {}),
    ...(contextFiles ? { contextFiles } : {}),
    ...(skills ? { skills } : {}),
    ...(agents ? { agents } : {}),
    ...(commands ? { commands } : {}),
    ...(policies ? { policies } : {}),
    ...(mcpServers ? { mcpServers } : {}),
    ...(settings ? { settings } : {}),
    ...(planDirectory !== undefined ? { planDirectory } : {}),
    ...(extensionFiles ? { extensionFiles } : {}),
  };
}

    });

    it('should correctly evaluate isEnabled without subdirs', () => {
      manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/*');
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/dir');
      expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test', '/path/to/dir')).toBe(true);
      expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test', '/path/to/dir/sub')).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('pruning child rules', () => {
    it('should remove child rules when enabling a parent with subdirs', () => {
      // Pre-existing rules for children
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/dir/subdir1');
      manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/path/to/dir/subdir2');
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/another/dir');

      // Enable the parent directory
      manager.enable('ext-test', true, '/path/to/dir');

      const config = manager.readConfig();
      const overrides = config['ext-test'].overrides;

      // The new parent rule should be present
      expect(overrides).toContain(`/path/to/dir/*`);

      // Child rules should be removed
      expect(overrides).not.toContain('/path/to/dir/subdir1/');
      expect(overrides).not.toContain(`!/path/to/dir/subdir2/*`);

      // Unrelated rules should remain
      expect(overrides).toContain('/path/to/another/dir/');
    });

    it('should remove child rules when disabling a parent with subdirs', () => {
      // Pre-existing rules for children
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/dir/subdir1');
      manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/path/to/dir/subdir2');
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/another/dir');

      // Disable the parent directory
      manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/path/to/dir');

      const config = manager.readConfig();
      const overrides = config['ext-test'].overrides;

      // The new parent rule should be present
      expect(overrides).toContain(`!/path/to/dir/*`);

      // Child rules should be removed
      expect(overrides).not.toContain('/path/to/dir/subdir1/');
      expect(overrides).not.toContain(`!/path/to/dir/subdir2/*`);

      // Unrelated rules should remain
      expect(overrides).toContain('/path/to/another/dir/');
    });

    it('should not remove child rules if includeSubdirs is false', () => {
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/dir/subdir1');
      manager.enable('ext-test', false, '/path/to/dir'); // Not including subdirs

      const config = manager.readConfig();
      const overrides = config['ext-test'].overrides;

      expect(overrides).toContain('/path/to/dir/subdir1/');
      expect(overrides).toContain('/path/to/dir/');
    });
  });

  it('should correctly prioritize more specific enable rules', () => {
    manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/Users/chrstn');
    manager.enable('ext-test', true, '/Users/chrstn/gemini-cli');

    expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test', '/Users/chrstn/gemini-cli')).toBe(
      true,
    );
  });

  it('should not disable subdirectories if includeSubdirs is false', () => {
    manager.disable('ext-test', false, '/Users/chrstn');
    expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test', '/Users/chrstn/gemini-cli')).toBe(
      true,
    );
  });

  describe('extension overrides (-e <name>)', () => {
    beforeEach(() => {
      manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager(['ext-test']);
    });

    it('can enable extensions, case-insensitive', () => {
      manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/');
      expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test', '/')).toBe(true);
      expect(manager.isEnabled('Ext-Test', '/')).toBe(true);
      // Double check that it would have been disabled otherwise
      expect(new ExtensionEnablementManager().isEnabled('ext-test', '/')).toBe(
        false,
      );
    });

    it('disable all other extensions', () => {
      manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager(['ext-test']);
      manager.enable('ext-test-2', true, '/');
      expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test-2', '/')).toBe(false);
      // Double check that it would have been enabled otherwise
      expect(
        new ExtensionEnablementManager().isEnabled('ext-test-2', '/'),
      ).toBe(true);
    });

    it('none disables all extensions', () => {
      manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager(['none']);
      manager.enable('ext-test', true, '/');
      expect(manager.isEnabled('ext-test', '/path/to/dir')).toBe(false);
      // Double check that it would have been enabled otherwise
      expect(new ExtensionEnablementManager().isEnabled('ext-test', '/')).toBe(
        true,
      );
    });
  });

  describe('validateExtensionOverrides', () => {
    let coreEventsEmitSpy: ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn>;

    beforeEach(() => {
      coreEventsEmitSpy = vi.spyOn(coreEvents, 'emitFeedback');
    });

    afterEach(() => {
      coreEventsEmitSpy.mockRestore();
    });

    it('should not log an error if enabledExtensionNamesOverride is empty', () => {
      const manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager([]);
      manager.validateExtensionOverrides([]);
      expect(coreEventsEmitSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('should not log an error if all enabledExtensionNamesOverride are valid', () => {
      const manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager(['ext-one', 'ext-two']);
      const extensions = [
        { name: 'ext-one' },
        { name: 'ext-two' },
      ] as GeminiCLIExtension[];
      manager.validateExtensionOverrides(extensions);
      expect(coreEventsEmitSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('should log an error for each invalid extension name in enabledExtensionNamesOverride', () => {
      const manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager([
        'ext-one',
        'ext-invalid',
        'ext-another-invalid',
      ]);
      const extensions = [
        { name: 'ext-one' },
        { name: 'ext-two' },
      ] as GeminiCLIExtension[];
      manager.validateExtensionOverrides(extensions);
      expect(coreEventsEmitSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
      expect(coreEventsEmitSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'error',
        'Extension not found: ext-invalid',
      );
      expect(coreEventsEmitSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'error',
        'Extension not found: ext-another-invalid',
      );
    });

    it('should not log an error if "none" is in enabledExtensionNamesOverride', () => {
      const manager = new ExtensionEnablementManager(['none']);
      manager.validateExtensionOverrides([]);
      expect(coreEventsEmitSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });
  });
});

describe('Override', () => {
  it('should create an override from input', () => {
    const override = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    expect(override.baseRule).toBe(`/path/to/dir/`);
    expect(override.isDisable).toBe(false);
    expect(override.includeSubdirs).toBe(true);
  });

  it('should create a disable override from input', () => {
    const override = Override.fromInput('!/path/to/dir', false);
    expect(override.baseRule).toBe(`/path/to/dir/`);
    expect(override.isDisable).toBe(true);
    expect(override.includeSubdirs).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should create an override from a file rule', () => {
    const override = Override.fromFileRule('/path/to/dir/');
    expect(override.baseRule).toBe('/path/to/dir/');
    expect(override.isDisable).toBe(false);
    expect(override.includeSubdirs).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should create an override from a file rule without a trailing slash', () => {
    const override = Override.fromFileRule('/path/to/dir');
    expect(override.baseRule).toBe('/path/to/dir');
    expect(override.isDisable).toBe(false);
    expect(override.includeSubdirs).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should create a disable override from a file rule', () => {
    const override = Override.fromFileRule('!/path/to/dir/');
    expect(override.isDisable).toBe(true);
    expect(override.baseRule).toBe('/path/to/dir/');
    expect(override.includeSubdirs).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should create an override with subdirs from a file rule', () => {
    const override = Override.fromFileRule('/path/to/dir/*');
    expect(override.baseRule).toBe('/path/to/dir/');
    expect(override.isDisable).toBe(false);
    expect(override.includeSubdirs).toBe(true);
  });

  it('should correctly identify conflicting overrides', () => {
    const override1 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const override2 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', false);
    expect(override1.conflictsWith(override2)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('should correctly identify non-conflicting overrides', () => {
    const override1 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const override2 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/another/dir', true);
    expect(override1.conflictsWith(override2)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should correctly identify equal overrides', () => {
    const override1 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const override2 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    expect(override1.isEqualTo(override2)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('should correctly identify unequal overrides', () => {
    const override1 = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const override2 = Override.fromInput('!/path/to/dir', true);
    expect(override1.isEqualTo(override2)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should generate the correct regex', () => {
    const override = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const regex = override.asRegex();
    expect(regex.test('/path/to/dir/')).toBe(true);
    expect(regex.test('/path/to/dir/subdir')).toBe(true);
    expect(regex.test('/path/to/another/dir')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should correctly identify child overrides', () => {
    const parent = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const child = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir/subdir', false);
    expect(child.isChildOf(parent)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('should correctly identify child overrides with glob', () => {
    const parent = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir/*', true);
    const child = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir/subdir', false);
    expect(child.isChildOf(parent)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('should correctly identify non-child overrides', () => {
    const parent = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    const other = Override.fromInput('/path/to/another/dir', false);
    expect(other.isChildOf(parent)).toBe(false);
  });

  it('should generate the correct output string', () => {
    const override = Override.fromInput('/path/to/dir', true);
    expect(override.output()).toBe(`/path/to/dir/*`);
  });

  it('should generate the correct output string for a disable override', () => {
    const override = Override.fromInput('!/path/to/dir', false);
    expect(override.output()).toBe(`!/path/to/dir/`);
  });

  it('should disable a path based on a disable override rule', () => {
    const override = Override.fromInput('!/path/to/dir', false);
    expect(override.output()).toBe(`!/path/to/dir/`);
  });
});

/**
 * @license
 * Copyright 2025 Google LLC
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
 */

import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { coreEvents, type GeminiCLIExtension } from '@google/gemini-cli-core';
import { ExtensionStorage } from './storage.js';
import { z } from 'zod';

export interface ExtensionEnablementConfig {
  overrides: string[];
}

export interface AllExtensionsEnablementConfig {
  [extensionName: string]: ExtensionEnablementConfig;
}

export class Override {
  constructor(
    public baseRule: string,
    public isDisable: boolean,
    public includeSubdirs: boolean,
  ) {}

  static fromInput(inputRule: string, includeSubdirs: boolean): Override {
    const isDisable = inputRule.startsWith('!');
    let baseRule = isDisable ? inputRule.substring(1) : inputRule;
    baseRule = ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash(baseRule);
    return new Override(baseRule, isDisable, includeSubdirs);
  }

  static fromFileRule(fileRule: string): Override {
    const isDisable = fileRule.startsWith('!');
    let baseRule = isDisable ? fileRule.substring(1) : fileRule;
    const includeSubdirs = baseRule.endsWith('*');
    baseRule = includeSubdirs
      ? baseRule.substring(0, baseRule.length - 1)
      : baseRule;
    return new Override(baseRule, isDisable, includeSubdirs);
  }

  conflictsWith(other: Override): boolean {
    if (this.baseRule === other.baseRule) {
      return (
        this.includeSubdirs !== other.includeSubdirs ||
        this.isDisable !== other.isDisable
      );
    }
    return false;
  }

  isEqualTo(other: Override): boolean {
    return (
      this.baseRule === other.baseRule &&
      this.includeSubdirs === other.includeSubdirs &&
      this.isDisable === other.isDisable
    );
  }

  asRegex(): RegExp {
    return globToRegex(`${this.baseRule}${this.includeSubdirs ? '*' : ''}`);
  }

  isChildOf(parent: Override) {
    if (!parent.includeSubdirs) {
      return false;
    }
    return parent.asRegex().test(this.baseRule);
  }

  output(): string {
    return `${this.isDisable ? '!' : ''}${this.baseRule}${this.includeSubdirs ? '*' : ''}`;
  }

  matchesPath(path: string) {
    return this.asRegex().test(path);
  }
}

const ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash = function (dirPath: string): string {
  // Normalize separators to forward slashes for consistent matching across platforms.
  let result = dirPath.replace(/\\/g, '/');
  if (result.charAt(0) !== '/') {
    result = '/' + result;
  }
  if (result.charAt(result.length - 1) !== '/') {
    result = result + '/';
  }
  return result;
};

/**
 * Converts a glob pattern to a RegExp object.
 * This is a simplified implementation that supports `*`.
 *
 * @param glob The glob pattern to convert.
 * @returns A RegExp object.
 */
function globToRegex(glob: string): RegExp {
  const regexString = glob
    .replace(/[.+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&') // Escape special regex characters
    .replace(/(\/?)\*/g, '($1.*)?'); // Convert * to optional group

  return new RegExp(`^${regexString}$`);
}

export class ExtensionEnablementManager {
  private configFilePath: string;
  private configDir: string;
  // If non-empty, this overrides all other extension configuration and enables
  // only the ones in this list.
  private enabledExtensionNamesOverride: string[];

  constructor(enabledExtensionNames?: string[]) {
    this.configDir = ExtensionStorage.getUserExtensionsDir();
    this.configFilePath = path.join(
      this.configDir,
      'extension-enablement.json',
    );
    this.enabledExtensionNamesOverride =
      enabledExtensionNames?.map((name) => name.toLowerCase()) ?? [];
  }

  validateExtensionOverrides(extensions: GeminiCLIExtension[]) {
    for (const name of this.enabledExtensionNamesOverride) {
      if (name === 'none') continue;
      if (
        !extensions.some((ext) => ext.name.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase())
      ) {
        coreEvents.emitFeedback('error', `Extension not found: ${name}`);
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * Determines if an extension is enabled based on its name and the current
   * path. The last matching rule in the overrides list wins.
   *
   * @param extensionName The name of the extension.
   * @param currentPath The absolute path of the current working directory.
   * @returns True if the extension is enabled, false otherwise.
   */
  isEnabled(extensionName: string, currentPath: string): boolean {
    // If we have a single override called 'none', this disables all extensions.
    // Typically, this comes from the user passing `-e none`.
    if (
      this.enabledExtensionNamesOverride.length === 1 &&
      this.enabledExtensionNamesOverride[0] === 'none'
    ) {
      return false;
    }

    // If we have explicit overrides, only enable those extensions.
    if (this.enabledExtensionNamesOverride.length > 0) {
      // When checking against overrides ONLY, we use a case insensitive match.
      // The override names are already lowercased in the constructor.
      return this.enabledExtensionNamesOverride.includes(
        extensionName.toLocaleLowerCase(),
      );
    }

    // Otherwise, we use the configuration settings
    const config = this.readConfig();
    const extensionConfig = config[extensionName];
    // Extensions are enabled by default.
    let enabled = true;
    const allOverrides = extensionConfig?.overrides ?? [];
    for (const rule of allOverrides) {
      const override = Override.fromFileRule(rule);
      if (override.matchesPath(ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash(currentPath))) {
        enabled = !override.isDisable;
      }
    }
    return enabled;
  }

  readConfig(): AllExtensionsEnablementConfig {
    try {
      const content = fs.readFileSync(this.configFilePath, 'utf-8');
      const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(content);
      const schema = z.record(
        z.string(),
        z.object({ overrides: z.array(z.string()) }),
      );
      return schema.parse(parsed);
    } catch (error) {
      if (
        error instanceof Error &&
        'code' in error &&
        error.code === 'ENOENT'
      ) {
        return {};
      }
      coreEvents.emitFeedback(
        'error',
        'Failed to read extension enablement config.',
        error,
      );
      return {};
    }
  }

  writeConfig(config: AllExtensionsEnablementConfig): void {
    fs.mkdirSync(this.configDir, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(this.configFilePath, JSON.stringify(config, null, 2));
  }

  enable(
    extensionName: string,
    includeSubdirs: boolean,
    scopePath: string,
  ): void {
    const config = this.readConfig();
    if (!config[extensionName]) {
      config[extensionName] = { overrides: [] };
    }
    const override = Override.fromInput(scopePath, includeSubdirs);
    const overrides = config[extensionName].overrides.filter((rule) => {
      const fileOverride = Override.fromFileRule(rule);
      if (
        fileOverride.conflictsWith(override) ||
        fileOverride.isEqualTo(override)
      ) {
        return false; // Remove conflicts and equivalent values.
      }
      return !fileOverride.isChildOf(override);
    });
    overrides.push(override.output());
    config[extensionName].overrides = overrides;
    this.writeConfig(config);
  }

  disable(
    extensionName: string,
    includeSubdirs: boolean,
    scopePath: string,
  ): void {
    this.enable(extensionName, includeSubdirs, `!${scopePath}`);
  }

  remove(extensionName: string): void {
    const config = this.readConfig();
    if (config[extensionName]) {
      delete config[extensionName];
      this.writeConfig(config);
    }
  }
}

      const userKeychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(
        `Gemini CLI Extensions test-ext 12345`,
      );
      await userKeychain.setSecret('SENSITIVE_VAR', 'secret');
      const envPath = path.join(extensionDir, '.env');
      await fsPromises.writeFile(envPath, 'VAR1=previous-VAR1');

      await maybePromptForSettings(
        newConfig,
        '12345',
        mockRequestSetting,
        previousConfig,
        previousSettings,
      );

      expect(mockRequestSetting).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      const actualContent = await fsPromises.readFile(envPath, 'utf-8');
      expect(actualContent).toBe('');
      expect(await userKeychain.getSecret('SENSITIVE_VAR')).toBeNull();
    });

    it('should remove sensitive settings from keychain', async () => {
      const previousConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.0.0',
        settings: [
          {
            name: 's1',

    it('should reprompt if a setting changes sensitivity', async () => {
      const previousConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',

      const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {

        settings: [

        ],
      };
      const previousSettings = { VAR1: 'previous-VAR1' };

      await maybePromptForSettings(
        newConfig,
        '12345',
        mockRequestSetting,
        previousConfig,
        previousSettings,
      );

      expect(mockRequestSetting).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      expect(mockRequestSetting).toHaveBeenCalledWith(newConfig.settings![0]);

      // The value should now be in keychain, not the .env file.
      const expectedEnvPath = path.join(extensionDir, '.env');
      const actualContent = await fsPromises.readFile(expectedEnvPath, 'utf-8');
      expect(actualContent).toBe('');
    });

    it('should not prompt if settings are identical', async () => {
      const previousConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.0.0',
        settings: [
          { name: 's1', description: 'd1', envVar: 'VAR1' },

      expect(actualContent).toBe(expectedContent);
    });

    it('should wrap values with spaces in quotes', async () => {

    });

    it('should not set sensitive settings if the value is empty during initial setup', async () => {

  describe('promptForSetting', () => {

    ])('$description', async ({ setting, expectedType, promptValue }) => {

  describe('getScopedEnvContents', () => {

  describe('updateSetting', () => {
    const config: ExtensionConfig = {
      name: 'test-ext',
      version: '1.0.0',
      settings: [
        { name: 's1', description: 'd1', envVar: 'VAR1' },
        { name: 's2', description: 'd2', envVar: 'VAR2', sensitive: true },

    beforeEach(async () => {

      );
    });

    it('should update a sensitive setting in USER scope', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('new-value2');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR2',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      const userKeychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(
        `Gemini CLI Extensions test-ext 12345`,
      );
      expect(await userKeychain.getSecret('VAR2')).toBe('new-value2');
    });

    it('should update a sensitive setting in WORKSPACE scope', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('new-workspace-secret');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR2',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.WORKSPACE,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      const workspaceKeychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(
        `Gemini CLI Extensions test-ext 12345 ${tempWorkspaceDir}`,
      );
      expect(await workspaceKeychain.getSecret('VAR2')).toBe(
        'new-workspace-secret',
      );
    });

    it('should leave existing, unmanaged .env variables intact when updating in WORKSPACE scope', async () => {
      // Setup a pre-existing .env file in the workspace with unmanaged variables
      const workspaceEnvPath = path.join(tempWorkspaceDir, '.env');
      const originalEnvContent =
        'PROJECT_VAR_1=value_1\nPROJECT_VAR_2=value_2\nVAR1=original-value'; // VAR1 is managed by extension
      await fsPromises.writeFile(workspaceEnvPath, originalEnvContent);

      // Simulate updating an extension-managed non-sensitive setting
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('updated-value');
      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR1',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.WORKSPACE,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      // Read the .env file after update
      const actualContent = await fsPromises.readFile(
        workspaceEnvPath,
        'utf-8',
      );

      // Assert that original variables are intact and extension variable is updated
      expect(actualContent).toContain('PROJECT_VAR_1=value_1');
      expect(actualContent).toContain('PROJECT_VAR_2=value_2');
      expect(actualContent).toContain('VAR1=updated-value');

      // Ensure no other unexpected changes or deletions
      const lines = actualContent.split('\n').filter((line) => line.length > 0);
      expect(lines).toHaveLength(3); // Should only have the three variables
    });

    it('should delete a sensitive setting if the new value is empty', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR2',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      const userKeychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(

      );
      expect(await userKeychain.getSecret('VAR2')).toBeNull();
    });

    it('should delete a non-sensitive setting if the new value is empty', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR1',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      const expectedEnvPath = path.join(extensionDir, '.env');
      const actualContent = await fsPromises.readFile(expectedEnvPath, 'utf-8');
      expect(actualContent).not.toContain('VAR1=');
    });

    it('should not throw if deleting a non-existent sensitive setting with empty value', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('');
      // Ensure it doesn't exist first
