        `Gemini CLI Extensions test-ext 12345`,
      );
      await userKeychain.deleteSecret('VAR2');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR2',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );
      // Should complete without error
    });

    it('should throw error if env var name contains invalid characters', async () => {
      const securityConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.0.0',
        settings: [{ name: 's2', description: 'd2', envVar: 'VAR-BAD' }],
      };
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('value');

      await expect(
        updateSetting(
          securityConfig,
          '12345',
          'VAR-BAD',
          mockRequestSetting,
          ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
          tempWorkspaceDir,
        ),
      ).rejects.toThrow(/Invalid environment variable name/);
    });

    it('should throw error if env var value contains newlines', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('value\nwith\nnewlines');

      await expect(
        updateSetting(
          config,
          '12345',
          'VAR1',
          mockRequestSetting,
          ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
          tempWorkspaceDir,
        ),
      ).rejects.toThrow(/Invalid environment variable value/);
    });

    it('should quote values with spaces', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('value with spaces');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR1',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      const expectedEnvPath = path.join(extensionDir, '.env');
      const actualContent = await fsPromises.readFile(expectedEnvPath, 'utf-8');
      expect(actualContent).toContain('VAR1="value with spaces"');
    });

    it('should escape quotes in values', async () => {
      mockRequestSetting.mockResolvedValue('value with "quotes"');

      await updateSetting(
        config,
        '12345',
        'VAR1',
        mockRequestSetting,
        ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
        tempWorkspaceDir,
      );

      const expectedEnvPath = path.join(extensionDir, '.env');
      const actualContent = await fsPromises.readFile(expectedEnvPath, 'utf-8');
      expect(actualContent).toContain('VAR1="value with \\"quotes\\""');
    });
  });
});

/**

 * Copyright 2025 Google LLC
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

import * as fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import * as fsSync from 'node:fs';
import * as dotenv from 'dotenv';
import * as path from 'node:path';

import { ExtensionStorage } from './storage.js';
import type { ExtensionConfig } from '../extension.js';

import prompts from 'prompts';
import { debugLogger, KeychainTokenStorage } from '@google/gemini-cli-core';
import { EXTENSION_SETTINGS_FILENAME } from './variables.js';

export enum ExtensionSettingScope {
  USER = 'user',
  WORKSPACE = 'workspace',
}

export interface ExtensionSetting {
  name: string;
  description: string;
  envVar: string;
  // NOTE: If no value is set, this setting will be considered NOT sensitive.
  sensitive?: boolean;
}

const getKeychainStorageName = (
  extensionName: string,
  extensionId: string,
  scope: ExtensionSettingScope,
  workspaceDir?: string,
): string => {
  const base = `Gemini CLI Extensions ${extensionName} ${extensionId}`;
  if (scope === ExtensionSettingScope.WORKSPACE) {
    if (!workspaceDir) {
      throw new Error('Workspace directory is required for workspace scope');
    }
    return `${base} ${workspaceDir}`;
  }
  return base;
};

export const getEnvFilePath = (
  extensionName: string,
  scope: ExtensionSettingScope,
  workspaceDir?: string,
): string => {
  if (scope === ExtensionSettingScope.WORKSPACE) {
    if (!workspaceDir) {
      throw new Error('Workspace directory is required for workspace scope');
    }
    return path.join(workspaceDir, EXTENSION_SETTINGS_FILENAME);
  }
  return new ExtensionStorage(extensionName).getEnvFilePath();
};

export async function maybePromptForSettings(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  extensionId: string,
  requestSetting: (setting: ExtensionSetting) => Promise<string | undefined>,
  previousExtensionConfig?: ExtensionConfig,
  previousSettings?: Record<string, string>,
): Promise<void> {
  const { name: extensionName, settings } = extensionConfig;
  if (
    (!settings || settings.length === 0) &&
    (!previousExtensionConfig?.settings ||
      previousExtensionConfig.settings.length === 0)
  ) {
    return;
  }
  // We assume user scope here because we don't have a way to ask the user for scope during the initial setup.
  // The user can change the scope later using the `settings set` command.
  const scope = ExtensionSettingScope.USER;
  const envFilePath = getEnvFilePath(extensionName, scope);
  const keychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(
    getKeychainStorageName(extensionName, extensionId, scope),
  );

  if (!settings || settings.length === 0) {
    await clearSettings(envFilePath, keychain);
    return;
  }

  const settingsChanges = getSettingsChanges(
    settings,
    previousExtensionConfig?.settings ?? [],
  );

  const allSettings: Record<string, string> = { ...previousSettings };

  for (const removedEnvSetting of settingsChanges.removeEnv) {
    delete allSettings[removedEnvSetting.envVar];
  }

  for (const removedSensitiveSetting of settingsChanges.removeSensitive) {
    await keychain.deleteSecret(removedSensitiveSetting.envVar);
  }

  for (const setting of settingsChanges.promptForSensitive.concat(
    settingsChanges.promptForEnv,
  )) {
    const answer = await requestSetting(setting);
    if (answer !== undefined) {
      allSettings[setting.envVar] = answer;
    }
  }

  const nonSensitiveSettings: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const setting of settings) {
    const value = allSettings[setting.envVar];
    if (value === undefined || value === '') {
      continue;
    }
    if (setting.sensitive) {
      await keychain.setSecret(setting.envVar, value);
    } else {
      nonSensitiveSettings[setting.envVar] = value;
    }
  }

  const envContent = formatEnvContent(nonSensitiveSettings);

  if (fsSync.existsSync(envFilePath)) {
    const stat = fsSync.statSync(envFilePath);
    if (stat.isDirectory()) {
      throw new Error(
        `Cannot write extension settings to ${envFilePath} because it is a directory.`,
      );
    }
  }

  await fs.writeFile(envFilePath, envContent);
}

function formatEnvContent(settings: Record<string, string>): string {
  let envContent = '';
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(settings)) {
    if (!/^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$/.test(key)) {
      throw new Error(
        `Invalid environment variable name: "${key}". Must contain only alphanumeric characters and underscores.`,
      );
    }
    if (value.includes('\n') || value.includes('\r')) {
      throw new Error(
        `Invalid environment variable value for "${key}". Values cannot contain newlines.`,
      );
    }
    const formattedValue = value.includes(' ')
      ? `"${value.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`
      : value;
    envContent += `${key}=${formattedValue}\n`;
  }
  return envContent;
}

export async function promptForSetting(
  setting: ExtensionSetting,
): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const response = await prompts({
    type: setting.sensitive ? 'password' : 'text',
    name: 'value',
    message: `${setting.name}\n${setting.description}`,
  });
  return typeof response.value === 'string' ? response.value : undefined;
}

export async function getScopedEnvContents(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  extensionId: string,
  scope: ExtensionSettingScope,
  workspaceDir?: string,
): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  const { name: extensionName } = extensionConfig;
  const keychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(
    getKeychainStorageName(extensionName, extensionId, scope, workspaceDir),
  );
  const envFilePath = getEnvFilePath(extensionName, scope, workspaceDir);
  let customEnv: Record<string, string> = {};
  if (fsSync.existsSync(envFilePath)) {
    const stat = fsSync.statSync(envFilePath);
    if (!stat.isDirectory()) {
      const envFile = fsSync.readFileSync(envFilePath, 'utf-8');
      customEnv = dotenv.parse(envFile);
    }
  }

  if (extensionConfig.settings) {
    for (const setting of extensionConfig.settings) {
      if (setting.sensitive) {
        const secret = await keychain.getSecret(setting.envVar);
        if (secret) {
          customEnv[setting.envVar] = secret;
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return customEnv;
}

export async function getEnvContents(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  extensionId: string,
  workspaceDir: string,
): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  if (!extensionConfig.settings || extensionConfig.settings.length === 0) {
    return Promise.resolve({});
  }

  const userSettings = await getScopedEnvContents(
    extensionConfig,
    extensionId,
    ExtensionSettingScope.USER,
  );
  const workspaceSettings = await getScopedEnvContents(
    extensionConfig,
    extensionId,
    ExtensionSettingScope.WORKSPACE,
    workspaceDir,
  );

  return { ...userSettings, ...workspaceSettings };
}

export async function updateSetting(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  extensionId: string,
  settingKey: string,
  requestSetting: (setting: ExtensionSetting) => Promise<string | undefined>,
  scope: ExtensionSettingScope,
  workspaceDir: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const { name: extensionName, settings } = extensionConfig;
  if (!settings || settings.length === 0) {
    debugLogger.log('This extension does not have any settings.');
    return;
  }

  const settingToUpdate = settings.find(
    (s) => s.name === settingKey || s.envVar === settingKey,
  );

  if (!settingToUpdate) {
    debugLogger.log(`Setting ${settingKey} not found.`);
    return;
  }

  const newValue = await requestSetting(settingToUpdate);
  if (newValue === undefined) {
    return;
  }

  const keychain = new KeychainTokenStorage(
    getKeychainStorageName(extensionName, extensionId, scope, workspaceDir),
  );

  if (settingToUpdate.sensitive) {
    if (newValue) {
      await keychain.setSecret(settingToUpdate.envVar, newValue);
    } else {
      try {
        await keychain.deleteSecret(settingToUpdate.envVar);
      } catch {
        // Ignore if secret does not exist
      }
    }
    return;
  }

  // For non-sensitive settings, we need to read the existing .env file,
  // update the value, and write it back, preserving any other values.
  const envFilePath = getEnvFilePath(extensionName, scope, workspaceDir);
  let envContent = '';
  if (fsSync.existsSync(envFilePath)) {
    const stat = fsSync.statSync(envFilePath);
    if (stat.isDirectory()) {
      throw new Error(
        `Cannot write extension settings to ${envFilePath} because it is a directory.`,
      );
    }
    envContent = await fs.readFile(envFilePath, 'utf-8');
  }

  const parsedEnv = dotenv.parse(envContent);
  if (!newValue) {
    delete parsedEnv[settingToUpdate.envVar];
  } else {
    parsedEnv[settingToUpdate.envVar] = newValue;
  }

  // We only want to write back the variables that are not sensitive.
  const nonSensitiveSettings: Record<string, string> = {};
  const sensitiveEnvVars = new Set(
    settings.filter((s) => s.sensitive).map((s) => s.envVar),
  );
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(parsedEnv)) {
    if (!sensitiveEnvVars.has(key)) {
      nonSensitiveSettings[key] = value;
    }
  }

  const newEnvContent = formatEnvContent(nonSensitiveSettings);
  await fs.writeFile(envFilePath, newEnvContent);
}

interface settingsChanges {
  promptForSensitive: ExtensionSetting[];
  removeSensitive: ExtensionSetting[];
  promptForEnv: ExtensionSetting[];
  removeEnv: ExtensionSetting[];
}
function getSettingsChanges(
  settings: ExtensionSetting[],
  oldSettings: ExtensionSetting[],
): settingsChanges {
  const isSameSetting = (a: ExtensionSetting, b: ExtensionSetting) =>
    a.envVar === b.envVar && (a.sensitive ?? false) === (b.sensitive ?? false);

  const sensitiveOld = oldSettings.filter((s) => s.sensitive ?? false);
  const sensitiveNew = settings.filter((s) => s.sensitive ?? false);
  const envOld = oldSettings.filter((s) => !(s.sensitive ?? false));
  const envNew = settings.filter((s) => !(s.sensitive ?? false));

  return {
    promptForSensitive: sensitiveNew.filter(
      (s) => !sensitiveOld.some((old) => isSameSetting(s, old)),
    ),
    removeSensitive: sensitiveOld.filter(
      (s) => !sensitiveNew.some((neu) => isSameSetting(s, neu)),
    ),
    promptForEnv: envNew.filter(
      (s) => !envOld.some((old) => isSameSetting(s, old)),
    ),
    removeEnv: envOld.filter(
      (s) => !envNew.some((neu) => isSameSetting(s, neu)),
    ),
  };
}

async function clearSettings(
  envFilePath: string,
  keychain: KeychainTokenStorage,
) {
  if (fsSync.existsSync(envFilePath)) {
    const stat = fsSync.statSync(envFilePath);
    if (!stat.isDirectory()) {
      await fs.writeFile(envFilePath, '');
    }
  }
  if (!(await keychain.isAvailable())) {
    return;
  }
  const secrets = await keychain.listSecrets();
  for (const secret of secrets) {
    await keychain.deleteSecret(secret);
  }
  return;
}

export async function getMissingSettings(
  extensionConfig: ExtensionConfig,
  extensionId: string,
  workspaceDir: string,
): Promise<ExtensionSetting[]> {
  const { settings } = extensionConfig;
  if (!settings || settings.length === 0) {
    return [];
  }

  const existingSettings = await getEnvContents(
    extensionConfig,
    extensionId,
    workspaceDir,
  );
  const missingSettings: ExtensionSetting[] = [];

  for (const setting of settings) {
    if (existingSettings[setting.envVar] === undefined) {
      missingSettings.push(setting);
    }
  }

  return missingSettings;
}

const EXTENSION_NAME = 'update-consent-fixture';
const isWindows = process.platform === 'win32';
const HOOK_V1 = 'echo hook-v1';
const HOOK_V2 = 'echo hook-v2-changed';

interface HookOptions {
  command: string;
  matcher?: string;
  env?: Record<string, string>;
}

interface SourceOptions {
  version: string;
  /** Extra fields for `gemini-extension.json`. */
  manifest?: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** Adds a `SessionStart` hook that runs this command. */
  hookCommand?: string;
  /** Adds a `SessionStart` hook with these options. */
  hook?: HookOptions;
  /** Raw content of `hooks/hooks.json`. */
  hooksFile?: string;
  context?: string;
  skillBody?: string;
  mcpServers?: Record<string, { command: string; args: string[] }>;
  /** Extra files, keyed by their path relative to the extension folder. */
  files?: Record<string, string>;
}

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

function hooksFileContent(hook: HookOptions): string {
  return JSON.stringify({
    hooks: {
      SessionStart: [
        {
          ...(hook.matcher !== undefined ? { matcher: hook.matcher } : {}),
          hooks: [
            {
              type: 'command',
              command: hook.command,
              ...(hook.env ? { env: hook.env } : {}),
            },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  });
}

function agentFile(body: string): string {
  return [
    '---',
    'name: release-helper',
    'description: Helps with releases',
    'mcp_servers:',
    '  tracker:',
    '    command: node',
    '    args:',
    '      - ${extensionPath}/servers/tracker.js',
    '    trust: true',
    '---',
    body,
  ].join('\n');
}

/** The MCP server layout of the `mcp-server` extension template. */
const MCP_TEMPLATE_MANIFEST = {

      command: 'node',

      cwd: '${extensionPath}',
    },
  },
};

/**
 * Runs git with a fixed identity and without the user's git settings.
 * `globalConfig` is an empty file that replaces the global git config. It is
 * a real file because Git for Windows can't read `os.devNull` (`\\.\nul`) as
 * a config file.
 */
function runGit(globalConfig: string, cwd: string, ...args: string[]): void {
  execFileSync(
    'git',
    [
      '-c',
      'user.name=Test',
      '-c',
      'user.email=test@example.com',
      '-c',
      'commit.gpgsign=false',
      ...args,
    ],
    {
      cwd,
      stdio: 'pipe',
      env: {
        ...process.env,
        GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: globalConfig,
        GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
      },
    },
  );
}

describe('extension update consent', () => {
  let tempHomeDir: string;
  let workspaceDir: string;
  let sourceDir: string;
  let userExtensionsDir: string;
  let requestConsent: MockedFunction<(consent: string) => Promise<boolean>>;
  let extensionManager: ExtensionManager;

  function createExtensionManager(hooksEnabled: boolean): ExtensionManager {
    const settings = createTestMergedSettings();
    settings.hooksConfig.enabled = hooksEnabled;

    const integrityManager: IExtensionIntegrity = {
      verify: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(IntegrityDataStatus.VERIFIED),
      store: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined),
    };

    return new ExtensionManager({
      workspaceDir,
      requestConsent,
      requestSetting: null,
      settings,
      integrityManager,
    });
  }

  /** Replaces the extension source folder with the files of one version. */
  function writeSource(options: SourceOptions): void {
    fs.rmSync(sourceDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
    fs.mkdirSync(sourceDir, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(
      path.join(sourceDir, 'gemini-extension.json'),
      JSON.stringify({
        name: EXTENSION_NAME,
        version: options.version,
        ...options.manifest,
        ...(options.mcpServers ? { mcpServers: options.mcpServers } : {}),
      }),
    );
    const hook =
      options.hook ??
      (options.hookCommand !== undefined
        ? { command: options.hookCommand }
        : undefined);
    const hooksFile =
      options.hooksFile ?? (hook ? hooksFileContent(hook) : undefined);
    if (hooksFile !== undefined) {
      fs.mkdirSync(path.join(sourceDir, 'hooks'));
      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(sourceDir, 'hooks', 'hooks.json'), hooksFile);
    }
    if (options.context !== undefined) {
      fs.writeFileSync(path.join(sourceDir, 'GEMINI.md'), options.context);
    }
    if (options.skillBody !== undefined) {
      const skillDir = path.join(sourceDir, 'skills', 'demo');
      fs.mkdirSync(skillDir, { recursive: true });
      fs.writeFileSync(
        path.join(skillDir, 'SKILL.md'),
        `---\nname: demo\ndescription: Demo skill\n---\n${options.skillBody}\n`,
      );
    }
    for (const [relativePath, content] of Object.entries(options.files ?? {})) {
      const filePath = path.join(sourceDir, relativePath);
      fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(filePath), { recursive: true });
      fs.writeFileSync(filePath, content);
    }
  }

  function installedFile(...segments: string[]): string {
    return path.join(userExtensionsDir, EXTENSION_NAME, ...segments);
  }

  function readInstalledVersion(): unknown {
    const manifest: unknown = JSON.parse(
      fs.readFileSync(installedFile('gemini-extension.json'), 'utf-8'),
    );
    return isRecord(manifest) ? manifest['version'] : undefined;
  }

  function readInstalledHookCommand(): string | undefined {
    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(
      fs.readFileSync(installedFile('hooks', 'hooks.json'), 'utf-8'),
    );
    if (!isRecord(parsed)) return undefined;
    const hooks = parsed['hooks'];
    if (!isRecord(hooks)) return undefined;
    const sessionStart = hooks['SessionStart'];
    if (!Array.isArray(sessionStart)) return undefined;
    const definition: unknown = sessionStart[0];
    if (!isRecord(definition)) return undefined;
    const entries = definition['hooks'];
    if (!Array.isArray(entries)) return undefined;
    const hook: unknown = entries[0];
    if (!isRecord(hook)) return undefined;
    const command = hook['command'];
    return typeof command === 'string' ? command : undefined;
  }

  /** Returns the text of the only consent request. */
  function consentText(): string {
    expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    return requestConsent.mock.calls[0][0];
  }

  /** Installs version 1.0.0 and checks that the install asked for consent. */
  async function installVersion1(
    options: Omit<SourceOptions, 'version'>,
  ): Promise<GeminiCLIExtension> {
    writeSource({ version: '1.0.0', ...options });
    await extensionManager.loadExtensions();
    const installed = await extensionManager.installOrUpdateExtension({
      source: sourceDir,
      type: 'local',
    });
    expect(
      requestConsent,
      'Precondition: the first install asks for consent once.',
    ).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    requestConsent.mockClear();
    return installed;
  }

  /**
   * Runs the same entry point as `gemini extensions update` and the
   * auto-update hook, and reports whether the update was applied.
   */
  async function settleUpdate(extension: GeminiCLIExtension): Promise<string> {
    try {
      await updateExtension(
        extension,
        extensionManager,
        ExtensionUpdateState.UPDATE_AVAILABLE,
        () => {},
      );
      return 'applied';
    } catch (error) {
      return `rejected: ${getErrorMessage(error)}`;
    }
  }

  beforeEach(() => {

  describe('hooks', () => {

      const outcome = await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    });

    it('does not ask for consent when unchanged hooks use ${extensionPath}', async () => {

    });

    it('asks for consent again when a script that a hook runs changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();

      expect(text).toContain('  * Hooks: `scripts/on-start.js` changed');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a file under hooks/ changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        hookCommand: HOOK_V1,
        files: { 'hooks/check.sh': 'echo check-v1' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        hookCommand: HOOK_V1,
        files: { 'hooks/check.sh': 'echo check-v2' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain('  * Hooks: `hooks/check.sh` changed');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when only a hook environment variable changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({

      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        hook: { command: HOOK_V1, env: { LOG_LEVEL: 'debug' } },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain('        - LOG_LEVEL: `debug`');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when only a hook matcher changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        hook: { command: HOOK_V1, matcher: 'startup' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        hook: { command: HOOK_V1, matcher: '*' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain(
        `  * SessionStart (matcher: \`*\`): \`${HOOK_V1}\``,
      );
    });

    it('asks for consent again, without failing, when hooks.json becomes malformed', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hooksFile: '{ "hooks": ' });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain(
        "`hooks/hooks.json` isn't a valid hooks file",
      );
    });

    it('compares hooks from the files when hooks are disabled in the settings', async () => {
      extensionManager = createExtensionManager(false);
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });

      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      expect(await settleUpdate(installed)).toBe('applied');
      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

      const updated = extensionManager
        .getExtensions()
        .find((extension) => extension.name === EXTENSION_NAME);
      if (!updated) {
        throw new Error('The updated extension is not loaded.');
      }
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.2', hookCommand: HOOK_V2 });
      await settleUpdate(updated);
      expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    });

    it('lists the new hook command above the question', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: HOOK_V2 });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toMatch(
        new RegExp(
          'Changes since the installed version:\\n' +
            '  \\* Hooks: new or changed `SessionStart: echo hook-v2-changed`$',
        ),
      );
    });

    it('shows a hook command with backticks, *, _, and $ verbatim in the interactive dialog', async () => {
      const command = 'echo `date` *bold* _under_ $HOME $\\to$';
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: command });
      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const { lastFrame, unmount } = await renderWithProviders(
        React.createElement(ConsentPrompt, {
          prompt: consentText(),
          onConfirm: vi.fn(),
          terminalWidth: 120,
        }),
      );

      expect(lastFrame()).toContain(`SessionStart: ${command}`);
      unmount();
    });
  });

  describe('context files', () => {
    it('asks for consent again when the GEMINI.md content changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ context: 'context v1' });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', context: 'context v2' });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(
        requestConsent,
        'Changed GEMINI.md content must trigger a consent request.',
      ).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain(
        'This extension will append info to your gemini.md context using GEMINI.md\n  Context files signature: ',
      );
      expect(text).toContain('  * Context files: `GEMINI.md` changed');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when GEMINI.md is added or removed', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({});
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', context: 'context' });
      expect(await settleUpdate(installed)).toBe('applied');
      expect(consentText()).toContain('  * Context files: `GEMINI.md` added');

      requestConsent.mockClear();
      const updated = extensionManager
        .getExtensions()
        .find((extension) => extension.name === EXTENSION_NAME);
      if (!updated) {
        throw new Error('The updated extension is not loaded.');
      }
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.2' });
      await settleUpdate(updated);
      expect(consentText()).toContain('  * Context files: `GEMINI.md` removed');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a file of a contextFileName list changes', async () => {
      const manifest = { contextFileName: ['a.md', 'b.md'] };
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        manifest,
        files: { 'a.md': 'a', 'b.md': 'b v1' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        manifest,
        files: { 'a.md': 'a', 'b.md': 'b v2' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain('  * Context files: `b.md` changed');
    });

    it('names a changed GEMINI.md under files, not context files, when contextFileName is set', async () => {
      const manifest = { contextFileName: 'CONTEXT.md' };
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        manifest,
        context: 'ignored v1',
        files: { 'CONTEXT.md': 'context' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        manifest,
        context: 'ignored v2',
        files: { 'CONTEXT.md': 'context' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain('context using CONTEXT.md');
      expect(text).toContain('  * Files: `GEMINI.md` changed');
      expect(text).not.toContain('Context files: `GEMINI.md`');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a file imported by GEMINI.md changes', async () => {
      const context = 'Follow @./docs/rules.md';
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        context,
        files: { 'docs/rules.md': 'rules v1' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        context,
        files: { 'docs/rules.md': 'rules v2' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain('  Imported files: `docs/rules.md`');
      expect(text).toContain('  * Context files: `docs/rules.md` changed');
    });

    it('does not ask for consent when context files are unchanged', async () => {
      const options = {
        context: 'Follow @./docs/rules.md',
        files: { 'docs/rules.md': 'rules' },
      };
      const installed = await installVersion1(options);
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', ...options });

      expect(await settleUpdate(installed)).toBe('applied');
      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });
  });

  describe('skills', () => {
    it('does not ask for consent when skills are unchanged', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ skillBody: 'body v1' });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', skillBody: 'body v1' });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(
        requestConsent,
        'Identical skills must not trigger a consent request.',
      ).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a skill file changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ skillBody: 'body v1' });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', skillBody: 'body v2' });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain('(Source: skills/demo/SKILL.md) (1 items');
      expect(text).toContain('  Skills signature: ');
      expect(text).toContain('  * Skills: `skills/demo` changed');
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a companion file of a skill changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({

    });
  });

  describe('sub-agents, custom commands, and policies', () => {
    it('asks for consent when a sub-agent with MCP servers is added, and shows its trust setting', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({});
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',

          'agents/release-helper.md': agentFile('Help with releases.'),
          'servers/tracker.js': 'server',
        },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain(
        [
          '  * `release-helper` (`agents/release-helper.md`)',
          '      MCP server `tracker` (local): `node ${extensionPath}/servers/tracker.js`',
          '      Trust: true',
        ].join('\n'),
      );
      expect(text).toContain(
        '  Files used by MCP servers: `servers/tracker.js`',
      );
      expect(text).toContain(
        '  * Sub-agents: `agents/release-helper.md` added',
      );
    });

    it('lists a remote sub-agent with its agent card URL', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({});
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        files: {
          'agents/remote.md':
            '---\nkind: remote\nname: remote-helper\nagent_card_url: https://example.com/card.json\n---\n',
        },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain(
        '  * `remote-helper` (`agents/remote.md`)\n      Agent card URL: `https://example.com/card.json`',
      );
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a sub-agent file changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        files: { 'agents/release-helper.md': agentFile('Version one.') },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        files: { 'agents/release-helper.md': agentFile('Version two.') },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain(
        '  * Sub-agents: `agents/release-helper.md` changed',
      );
    });

    it('names a changed file starting with _ in agents/ under files, not sub-agents', async () => {
      const files = { 'agents/release-helper.md': agentFile('Help.') };
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        files: { ...files, 'agents/_notes.md': 'notes v1' },

      writeSource({

      const text = consentText();

      expect(text).not.toContain('Sub-agents: `agents/_notes.md`');

    it.each([
      ['a nested folder', 'commands/release/notes.toml'],

  describe('MCP servers', () => {

      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    it('asks for consent again when the script of an MCP server changes', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        manifest: MCP_TEMPLATE_MANIFEST,
        files: { 'example.js': 'console.log("v1");' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        manifest: MCP_TEMPLATE_MANIFEST,
        files: { 'example.js': 'console.log("v2");' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain(
        '  * nodeServer (local): node ${extensionPath}/example.js\n    Working directory: ${extensionPath}',

      expect(text).toContain(
        '    Files used: `.` (the extension folder), `example.js`',

      expect(text).toContain('  * MCP servers: `example.js` changed');

    it('asks for consent again when a file in the working directory of an MCP server changes', async () => {

  describe('whole extension', () => {
    it('does not ask for consent for a version-only update when every kind of content is present', async () => {
      const options: Omit<SourceOptions, 'version'> = {
        manifest: MCP_TEMPLATE_MANIFEST,
        hookCommand: ON_START_COMMAND,
        context: 'Follow @./docs/rules.md',
        skillBody: 'body',
        files: {
          'example.js': 'console.log("server");',
          'scripts/on-start.js': 'console.log("start");',
          'docs/rules.md': 'rules',
          'agents/release-helper.md': agentFile('Help with releases.'),
          'servers/tracker.js': 'tracker',
          'commands/release/notes.toml': 'prompt = "notes"',
          'policies/release.toml': '# release policy',
        },
      };
      const installed = await installVersion1(options);
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', ...options });

      expect(await settleUpdate(installed)).toBe('applied');
      expect(requestConsent).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('asks for consent again when a module that a hook script loads changes', async () => {
      const hookCommand = 'node ${extensionPath}/scripts/hook.js';
      const hookScript = "require('./lib.js');";
      const installed = await installVersion1({
        hookCommand,
        files: { 'scripts/hook.js': hookScript, 'scripts/lib.js': 'v1' },
      });
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        hookCommand,
        files: { 'scripts/hook.js': hookScript, 'scripts/lib.js': 'v2' },
      });

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      const text = consentText();
      expect(text).toContain('Extension files signature: ');
      expect(text).toContain('  * Files: `scripts/lib.js` changed');
    });

    it.skipIf(isWindows)(
      'keeps relative links inside a local install, so the hooks signature covers their targets',
      async () => {
        const writeVersion = (version: string, script: string) => {
          writeSource({
            version,
            hookCommand: HOOK_V1,
            files: { 'shared/run.sh': script },
          });
          fs.symlinkSync(
            '../shared/run.sh',
            path.join(sourceDir, 'hooks', 'run.sh'),
          );
        };
        writeVersion('1.0.0', 'echo v1');
        await extensionManager.loadExtensions();
        const installed = await extensionManager.installOrUpdateExtension({
          source: sourceDir,
          type: 'local',
        });
        requestConsent.mockClear();

        expect(fs.readlinkSync(installedFile('hooks', 'run.sh'))).toBe(
          '../shared/run.sh',
        );

        writeVersion('1.0.1', 'echo v2');
        await settleUpdate(installed);

        expect(consentText()).toContain('  * Hooks: `hooks/run.sh` changed');
      },
    );

    it('asks for consent again when a hook command changes in an update from a git repository', async () => {
      const gitConfig = path.join(tempHomeDir, 'empty.gitconfig');
      fs.writeFileSync(gitConfig, '');
      const repoDir = path.join(tempHomeDir, 'remote', 'repo.git');
      fs.mkdirSync(repoDir, { recursive: true });
      runGit(gitConfig, repoDir, 'init', '--bare', '--initial-branch=main');
      const publish = (options: SourceOptions) => {
        writeSource(options);
        runGit(gitConfig, sourceDir, 'init', '--initial-branch=main');
        runGit(gitConfig, sourceDir, 'add', '-A');
        runGit(
          gitConfig,
          sourceDir,
          'commit',
          '-m',
          `Version ${options.version}`,
        );
        runGit(gitConfig, sourceDir, 'push', '--force', repoDir, 'HEAD:main');
      };

      publish({ version: '1.0.0', hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      await extensionManager.loadExtensions();
      const installed = await extensionManager.installOrUpdateExtension({
        source: pathToFileURL(repoDir).href,
        type: 'git',
      });
      requestConsent.mockClear();
      publish({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: HOOK_V2 });
      expect(
        await checkForExtensionUpdate(installed, extensionManager),
        'Precondition: the update check finds the new commit.',
      ).toBe(ExtensionUpdateState.UPDATE_AVAILABLE);

      await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(consentText()).toContain(
        '  * Hooks: new or changed `SessionStart: echo hook-v2-changed`',
      );
    });
  });

  describe('local sources', () => {
    it('installs the files that the consent text describes when the source changes during an update prompt', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: HOOK_V2 });
      requestConsent.mockImplementation(async () => {
        writeSource({ version: '1.0.2', hookCommand: 'echo hook-v3-late' });
        return true;
      });

      expect(await settleUpdate(installed)).toBe('applied');

      expect(consentText()).toContain(`  * SessionStart: \`${HOOK_V2}\``);
      expect(readInstalledHookCommand()).toBe(HOOK_V2);
      expect(readInstalledVersion()).toBe('1.0.1');
      const metadata: unknown = JSON.parse(
        fs.readFileSync(installedFile(INSTALL_METADATA_FILENAME), 'utf-8'),
      );
      expect(metadata).toMatchObject({ source: sourceDir, type: 'local' });
    });

    it('installs the files that the consent text describes when the source changes during a first install prompt', async () => {
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.0', hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      requestConsent.mockImplementation(async () => {
        writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: HOOK_V2 });
        return true;
      });
      await extensionManager.loadExtensions();

      await extensionManager.installOrUpdateExtension({
        source: sourceDir,
        type: 'local',
      });

      expect(consentText()).toContain(`  * SessionStart: \`${HOOK_V1}\``);
      expect(readInstalledHookCommand()).toBe(HOOK_V1);
      expect(readInstalledVersion()).toBe('1.0.0');
    });
  });

  describe('declined updates', () => {
    it('rejects with the consent message, keeps the ERROR state, and restores nothing', async () => {
      const errorSpy = vi.spyOn(debugLogger, 'error');
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      requestConsent.mockResolvedValue(false);
      writeSource({ version: '1.0.1', hookCommand: HOOK_V2 });
      const dispatch = vi.fn();

      await expect(
        updateExtension(
          installed,
          extensionManager,
          ExtensionUpdateState.UPDATE_AVAILABLE,
          dispatch,
        ),
      ).rejects.toThrow(
        /^Installation cancelled for "update-consent-fixture"\.$/,
      );

      expect(dispatch).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({
        type: 'SET_STATE',
        payload: { name: EXTENSION_NAME, state: ExtensionUpdateState.ERROR },
      });
      expect(errorSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.stringContaining('rolling back'),
      );
      expect(readInstalledHookCommand()).toBe(HOOK_V1);
    });
  });

  describe('interactive dialog', () => {
    it('declines when Enter is pressed in a dialog that selects "No" first', async () => {
      const onConfirm = vi.fn();
      const { stdin, waitUntilReady, unmount } = await renderWithProviders(
        React.createElement(ConsentPrompt, {
          prompt: 'Install this extension?',
          onConfirm,
          terminalWidth: 80,
          defaultToNo: true,
        }),
      );

      await act(async () => {
        stdin.write('\r');
      });
      await waitUntilReady();

      await vi.waitFor(() => expect(onConfirm).toHaveBeenCalledWith(false));
      unmount();
    });
  });

  describe('manifest changes', () => {
    it('asks for consent and keeps the installed version when an MCP server is added', async () => {
      const installed = await installVersion1({ hookCommand: HOOK_V1 });
      requestConsent.mockResolvedValue(false);
      writeSource({
        version: '1.0.1',
        hookCommand: HOOK_V1,
        mcpServers: { demo: { command: 'node', args: ['server.js'] } },
      });

      const outcome = await settleUpdate(installed);

      expect(requestConsent).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.stringContaining(
          'This extension will run the following MCP servers',
        ),
      );
      expect(outcome).toMatch(/^rejected: [\s\S]*Installation cancelled/);
      expect(readInstalledVersion()).toBe('1.0.0');
    });
  });
});

      const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.1.0',
        settings: [{ name: 's1', description: 'd1', envVar: 'VAR1' }],
      };

      const previousConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.0.0',
        settings: [],
      };

      const installMetadata: ExtensionInstallMetadata = {
        source: '/mock/source',
        type: 'local',
        autoUpdate: true,
      };

      // 2. Setup Manager
      const manager = new ExtensionManager({
        workspaceDir: tempWorkspaceDir,
        settings: createTestMergedSettings({
          telemetry: { enabled: false },
          experimental: { extensionConfig: true },
        }),
        requestConsent: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true),
        requestSetting: null,
      });

      // 3. Mock Internal Manager Methods
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'loadExtensionConfig').mockResolvedValue(newConfig);
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'getExtensions').mockReturnValue([
        {
          name: 'test-ext',
          version: '1.0.0',
          installMetadata,
          path: '/mock/extensions/test-ext',
          contextFiles: [],
          mcpServers: {},
          hooks: undefined,
          isActive: true,
          id: 'test-id',
          settings: [],
          resolvedSettings: [],
          skills: [],
        } as unknown as GeminiCLIExtension,
      ]);
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'uninstallExtension').mockResolvedValue(undefined);
      // Mock loadExtension to return something so the method doesn't crash at the end
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'loadExtension').mockResolvedValue({
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.1.0',
      } as unknown as GeminiCLIExtension);

      // 4. Mock External Helpers
      // This is the key fix: we explicitly mock `getMissingSettings` to return
      // the result we expect, avoiding any real FS or logic execution during the update.
      vi.mocked(getMissingSettings).mockResolvedValue([
        {
          name: 's1',
          description: 'd1',
          envVar: 'VAR1',
        },
      ]);

      // 5. Execute
      await manager.installOrUpdateExtension(installMetadata, previousConfig);

      // 6. Assert
      expect(debugLogger.warn).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.stringContaining(
          'Extension "test-ext" has missing settings: s1',
        ),
      );
      expect(coreEvents.emitFeedback).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'warning',
        expect.stringContaining(
          'Please run "gemini extensions config test-ext [setting-name]"',
        ),
      );
    });

    it('should store integrity data after update', async () => {
      const newConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.1.0',
      };

      const previousConfig: ExtensionConfig = {
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.0.0',
      };

      const installMetadata: ExtensionInstallMetadata = {
        source: '/mock/source',
        type: 'local',
      };

      const manager = new ExtensionManager({
        workspaceDir: tempWorkspaceDir,
        settings: createTestMergedSettings(),
        requestConsent: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(true),
        requestSetting: null,
      });

      await manager.loadExtensions();
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'loadExtensionConfig').mockResolvedValue(newConfig);
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'getExtensions').mockReturnValue([
        {
          name: 'test-ext',
          version: '1.0.0',
          installMetadata,
          path: '/mock/extensions/test-ext',
          isActive: true,
        } as unknown as GeminiCLIExtension,
      ]);
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'uninstallExtension').mockResolvedValue(undefined);
      vi.spyOn(manager, 'loadExtension').mockResolvedValue({
        name: 'test-ext',
        version: '1.1.0',
      } as unknown as GeminiCLIExtension);

      const storeSpy = vi.spyOn(manager, 'storeExtensionIntegrity');
      const releaseLock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);
      vi.mocked(lock).mockResolvedValueOnce(releaseLock);

      await manager.installOrUpdateExtension(installMetadata, previousConfig);

      expect(storeSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('test-ext', installMetadata);
      // The update ran under the extension's install lock, and released it.
      expect(lock).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        '/mock/extensions/test-ext',
        expect.objectContaining({
          realpath: false,
        }),
      );
      expect(releaseLock).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    });
  });
});

describe('github.ts', () => {
  function createMockResponse(
    statusCode = 200,
    headers: Record<string, string> = {},
    complete = true,
  ): IncomingMessage & PassThrough {
    const stream = new PassThrough();
    return Object.assign(stream, {
      statusCode,
      headers,
      complete,
    }) as unknown as IncomingMessage & PassThrough;
  }

  function createMockWriteStream(): fs.WriteStream {
    return new PassThrough() as unknown as fs.WriteStream;
  }

  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.resetAllMocks();
    vi.stubEnv('GITHUB_TOKEN', '');
    vi.mocked(validateUrlDestination).mockResolvedValue(true);
    vi.mocked(fs.promises.rename).mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    vi.mocked(fs.promises.unlink).mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    vi.unstubAllEnvs();
    vi.restoreAllMocks();
  });

  describe('cloneFromGit', () => {
    let mockGit: {
      clone: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
      getRemotes: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
      fetch: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
      checkout: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
      listRemote: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
      revparse: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
      env: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
    };

    beforeEach(() => {
      mockGit = {
        clone: vi.fn(),
        getRemotes: vi.fn(),
        fetch: vi.fn(),
        checkout: vi.fn(),
        listRemote: vi.fn(),
        revparse: vi.fn(),
        env: vi.fn().mockReturnThis(),
      };
      vi.mocked(simpleGit).mockReturnValue(mockGit as unknown as SimpleGit);
    });

    it('should clone, fetch and checkout a repo', async () => {
      mockGit.getRemotes.mockResolvedValue([{ name: 'origin' }]);

      await cloneFromGit(
        {
          type: 'git',
          source: 'https://github.com/owner/repo.git',
          ref: 'v1.0.0',
        },
        '/dest',
      );

      expect(mockGit.clone).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'https://github.com/owner/repo.git',
        './',
        ['--depth', '1'],
      );
      expect(mockGit.fetch).toHaveBeenCalledWith('origin', 'v1.0.0');
      expect(mockGit.checkout).toHaveBeenCalledWith('FETCH_HEAD');
    });

    it('should throw if no remotes found', async () => {
      mockGit.getRemotes.mockResolvedValue([]);

      await expect(
        cloneFromGit({ type: 'git', source: 'src' }, '/dest'),
      ).rejects.toThrow('Unable to find any remotes');
    });

    it('should throw on clone error', async () => {
      mockGit.clone.mockRejectedValue(new Error('Clone failed'));

      await expect(
        cloneFromGit({ type: 'git', source: 'src' }, '/dest'),
      ).rejects.toThrow('Failed to clone Git repository');
    });
  });

  describe('tryParseGithubUrl', () => {
    it.each([
      ['https://github.com/owner/repo', 'owner', 'repo'],
      ['https://github.com/owner/repo.git', 'owner', 'repo'],
      ['git@github.com:owner/repo.git', 'owner', 'repo'],
      ['owner/repo', 'owner', 'repo'],
    ])('should parse %s to %s/%s', (url, owner, repo) => {
      expect(tryParseGithubUrl(url)).toEqual({ owner, repo });
    });

    it.each([
      // `.git` inside the repo name must be preserved.
      ['https://github.com/someuser/blog.github.io', 'blog.github.io'],
      ['https://github.com/someuser/my.git.repo', 'my.git.repo'],
      // Only a trailing `.git` suffix is stripped, case-insensitively.
      ['https://github.com/someuser/tool.git', 'tool'],
      ['https://github.com/someuser/tool.GIT', 'tool'],
      ['https://github.com/someuser/blog.github.io.git', 'blog.github.io'],
    ])('should strip only a trailing .git suffix: %s -> %s', (url, repo) => {
      expect(tryParseGithubUrl(url)).toEqual({ owner: 'someuser', repo });
    });

    it.each([
      'https://gitlab.com/owner/repo',
      'https://my-git-host.com/owner/group/repo',
      'git@gitlab.com:some-group/some-project/some-repo.git',
    ])('should return null for non-GitHub URLs', (url) => {
      expect(tryParseGithubUrl(url)).toBeNull();
    });

    it('should throw for invalid formats', () => {
      expect(() => tryParseGithubUrl('invalid')).toThrow(
        'Invalid GitHub repository source',
      );
    });
  });

  describe('fetchReleaseFromGithub', () => {

  describe('downloadFromGitHubRelease', () => {
    it('should fail if no release data found', async () => {
      // Mock fetchJson to throw for latest release check
      vi.mocked(fetchJson).mockRejectedValue(new Error('Not found'));

      const result = await downloadFromGitHubRelease(
        {
          type: 'github-release',
          source: 'owner/repo',
          ref: 'v1',
        } as unknown as ExtensionInstallMetadata,
        '/dest',
        { owner: 'owner', repo: 'repo' },
      );

      expect(result.success).toBe(false);
      if (!result.success) {
        expect(result.failureReason).toBe('failed to fetch release data');
      }
    });

    it('should use correct headers for release assets', async () => {
      vi.mocked(fetchJson).mockResolvedValue({
        tag_name: 'v1.0.0',
        assets: [
          { name: 'asset.tar.gz', url: 'https://example.com/asset.tar.gz' },
        ],
      });
      vi.mocked(os.platform).mockReturnValue('linux');
      vi.mocked(os.arch).mockReturnValue('x64');

      // Mock https.get and fs.createWriteStream for downloadFile
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') {
          cb = options;
        }
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      // Mock fs.promises.readdir to return empty array (no cleanup needed)
      vi.mocked(fs.promises.readdir).mockResolvedValue([]);
      // Mock fs.promises.unlink
      vi.mocked(fs.promises.unlink).mockResolvedValue(undefined);

      const promise = downloadFromGitHubRelease(
        {
          type: 'github-release',
          source: 'owner/repo',
          ref: 'v1.0.0',
        } as unknown as ExtensionInstallMetadata,
        '/dest',
        { owner: 'owner', repo: 'repo' },
      );

      // Wait for downloadFile to be called and stream to be created
      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );

      // Complete response stream to finish pipeline
      mockRes.end('archive-bytes');

      await promise;

      expect(https.get).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'https://example.com/asset.tar.gz',
        expect.objectContaining({
          headers: expect.objectContaining({
            Accept: 'application/octet-stream',
          }),
        }),
        expect.anything(),
      );
    });

    it('should use correct headers for source tarballs', async () => {
      vi.mocked(fetchJson).mockResolvedValue({
        tag_name: 'v1.0.0',
        assets: [],
        tarball_url: 'https://example.com/tarball.tar.gz',
      });

      // Mock https.get and fs.createWriteStream for downloadFile
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') {
          cb = options;
        }
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      // Mock fs.promises.readdir to return empty array
      vi.mocked(fs.promises.readdir).mockResolvedValue([]);
      // Mock fs.promises.unlink
      vi.mocked(fs.promises.unlink).mockResolvedValue(undefined);

      const promise = downloadFromGitHubRelease(
        {
          type: 'github-release',
          source: 'owner/repo',
          ref: 'v1.0.0',
        } as unknown as ExtensionInstallMetadata,
        '/dest',
        { owner: 'owner', repo: 'repo' },
      );

      // Wait for downloadFile to be called and stream to be created
      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );

      // Complete response stream to finish pipeline
      mockRes.end('tarball-bytes');

      await promise;

      expect(https.get).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        'https://example.com/tarball.tar.gz',
        expect.objectContaining({
          headers: expect.objectContaining({
            Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json',
          }),
        }),
        expect.anything(),
      );
    });

    it('should return failed to download asset when download stream errors', async () => {
      vi.mocked(fetchJson).mockResolvedValue({
        tag_name: 'v1.0.0',
        assets: [
          { name: 'asset.tar.gz', url: 'https://example.com/asset.tar.gz' },
        ],
      });
      vi.mocked(os.platform).mockReturnValue('linux');
      vi.mocked(os.arch).mockReturnValue('x64');

      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') {
          cb = options;
        }
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      const promise = downloadFromGitHubRelease(
        {
          type: 'github-release',
          source: 'owner/repo',
          ref: 'v1.0.0',
        } as unknown as ExtensionInstallMetadata,
        '/dest',
        { owner: 'owner', repo: 'repo' },
      );

      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );

      mockStream.emit('error', new Error('ENOSPC: no space left on device'));

      const result = await promise;
      expect(result).toEqual({
        failureReason: 'failed to download asset',
        success: false,
        type: 'github-release',
        tagName: 'v1.0.0',
        errorMessage: expect.stringContaining(
          'ENOSPC: no space left on device',
        ),
      });
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });
  });

  describe('findReleaseAsset', () => {
    it('should find platform/arch specific asset', () => {
      vi.mocked(os.platform).mockReturnValue('darwin');
      vi.mocked(os.arch).mockReturnValue('arm64');
      const assets = [
        { name: 'darwin.arm64.tar.gz', url: 'url1' },
        { name: 'linux.x64.tar.gz', url: 'url2' },
      ];
      expect(findReleaseAsset(assets)).toEqual(assets[0]);
    });

    it('should find generic asset', () => {
      vi.mocked(os.platform).mockReturnValue('darwin');
      const assets = [{ name: 'generic.tar.gz', url: 'url' }];
      expect(findReleaseAsset(assets)).toEqual(assets[0]);
    });
  });

  describe('downloadFile', () => {
    const assetUrl = 'https://example.com/asset.tar.gz';
    const redirectedAssetUrl = 'https://example.com/redirected-asset.tar.gz';

    it('should download file successfully via temporary file and atomic rename', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') {
          cb = options;
        }
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      const promise = downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest');
      mockRes.end('file-contents');

      await expect(promise).resolves.toBeUndefined();
      expect(fs.createWriteStream).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(tempPath).toMatch(/^\/dest\..+\.tmp$/);
      expect(fs.promises.rename).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath, '/dest');

    it('should connect through a lookup that refuses private addresses', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementationOnce((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;

      await promise;

      const options = vi.mocked(https.get).mock.calls[0][1];
      if (!options || typeof options === 'function' || !options.lookup) {
        throw new Error('https.get was called without a lookup');
      }
      const resolveHost = promisify(options.lookup);

      await expect(resolveHost('10.0.0.5', {})).rejects.toThrow(PrivateIpError);

    it('should include Authorization header only for https github.com and *.github.com URLs', async () => {

    it('should strip Authorization header when redirecting from GitHub to an external asset host', async () => {

    it('should pass custom headers', async () => {

    it('should reject and remove partial temp file when response stream emits an error', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );
      mockRes.write('partial-bytes');
      mockRes.emit('error', new Error('Mid-transfer connection reset'));

      await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('Mid-transfer connection reset');
      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(mockStream.destroyed).toBe(true);
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath);
    });

    it('should reject, tear down response stream, and remove partial temp file when write stream emits an error', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {

      expect(mockRes.destroyed).toBe(true);

    });

    it('should reject and remove partial temp file when response closes prematurely before end', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;

      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath);
    });

    it('should reject and remove partial temp file when response ends with complete === false', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200, {}, false);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      const promise = downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest');
      mockRes.end('truncated-bytes');

      await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(
        `Response ended prematurely while downloading ${assetUrl}`,
      );
      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath);
    });

    it('should settle once with the first error when multiple failures occur', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      const promise = downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest');
      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );
      mockStream.emit('error', new Error('First failure: EACCES'));
      mockRes.emit('error', new Error('Second failure: socket reset'));
      mockReq.emit('error', new Error('Third failure: request aborted'));

      await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('First failure: EACCES');
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    });

    it('should clean up temp file if renaming to destination fails', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);
      vi.mocked(fs.promises.rename).mockRejectedValueOnce(
        new Error('EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory'),
      );

      const promise = downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest');
      mockRes.end('complete-bytes');

      await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(
        'EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory',
      );
      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath);
    });

    it('should reject, destroy response stream, and remove partial temp file when request emits an error mid-download', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      const promise = downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest');
      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );
      mockRes.write('partial-bytes');
      mockReq.emit('error', new Error('ECONNRESET: socket hang up'));

      await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('ECONNRESET: socket hang up');
      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(mockRes.destroyed).toBe(true);
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath);
    });

    it('should configure a 30000ms timeout, destroy request, and reject when request times out before response', async () => {
      const destroyMock = vi.fn();
      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementationOnce((_url, options) => {
        expect(options).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            timeout: 30000,
          }),
        );
        const req = Object.assign(new EventEmitter(), {
          destroy: destroyMock,
        }) as unknown as ClientRequest;
        queueMicrotask(() => {
          req.emit('timeout');
          req.emit('error', new Error('socket hang up'));
        });
        return req;
      });

      await expect(downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest')).rejects.toThrow(
        'Request timed out after 30000ms',
      );
      expect(destroyMock).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('should destroy response stream and remove partial temp file when request times out mid-download', async () => {
      const destroyMock = vi.fn();
      const mockReq = Object.assign(new EventEmitter(), {
        destroy: destroyMock,
      });
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementationOnce((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      const promise = downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest');
      await vi.waitUntil(
        () => vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls.length > 0,
      );
      mockRes.write('partial-bytes');
      mockReq.emit('timeout');

      await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow('Request timed out after 30000ms');
      const tempPath = vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mock.calls[0][0];
      expect(destroyMock).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      expect(mockRes.destroyed).toBe(true);
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledWith(tempPath);
    });

    it('should ignore late errors and timeouts on original request and response once a redirect has started', async () => {
      const destroyMock = vi.fn();
      const originalReq = Object.assign(new EventEmitter(), {
        destroy: destroyMock,
      });
      const mockResRedirect = createMockResponse(302, {
        location: redirectedAssetUrl,
      });
      const mockResSuccess = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get)
        .mockImplementationOnce((url, options, cb) => {
          if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
          queueMicrotask(() => {
            if (cb) cb(mockResRedirect);
          });
          return originalReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
        })
        .mockImplementationOnce((url, options, cb) => {
          // Emit late timeout and errors on original request and drained redirect response while redirect is in flight
          originalReq.emit('timeout');
          originalReq.emit('error', new Error('late original req error'));
          mockResRedirect.emit('error', new Error('late redirect drain error'));
          if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
          queueMicrotask(() => {
            if (cb) cb(mockResSuccess);
            mockResSuccess.end('redirected-contents');
          });
          return new EventEmitter() as unknown as ClientRequest;
        });

      const mockStream = createMockWriteStream();
      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockReturnValue(mockStream);

      await expect(downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest')).resolves.toBeUndefined();
      expect(destroyMock).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      expect(fs.promises.rename).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('should reject and destroy response if createWriteStream throws synchronously', async () => {
      const mockReq = new EventEmitter();
      const mockRes = createMockResponse(200);

      vi.mocked(https.get).mockImplementation((url, options, cb) => {
        if (typeof options === 'function') cb = options;
        if (cb) cb(mockRes);
        return mockReq as unknown as ClientRequest;
      });

      vi.mocked(fs.createWriteStream).mockImplementation(() => {
        throw new Error('ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: invalid path');
      });

      await expect(downloadFile(assetUrl, '/dest')).rejects.toThrow(
        'ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: invalid path',
      );
      expect(mockRes.destroyed).toBe(true);
      expect(fs.promises.rename).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect(fs.promises.unlink).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    });
  });

  describe('extractFile', () => {
    it('should extract tar.gz using tar', async () => {
      await extractFile('file.tar.gz', '/dest');
      expect(tar.x).toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('should extract zip using extract-zip', async () => {
      vi.mocked(extract.default || extract).mockResolvedValue(undefined);
      await extractFile('file.zip', '/dest');
      // Check if extract was called. Note: extract-zip export might be default or named depending on mock
    });

    it('should throw for unsupported extensions', async () => {
      await expect(extractFile('file.txt', '/dest')).rejects.toThrow(
        'Unsupported file extension',
      );
    });
  });
});

import { ExtensionUpdateState } from '../../ui/state/extensions.js';
import * as crypto from 'node:crypto';

  fetchJson,
  getGitHubToken,
  isTrustedGitHubUrl,
